item.title: Caiado e Zema anunciam apoio a Flávio na disputa com Lula no 2º turno da eleição
item.description: A assessoria do ex-governador de Goiás Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) informou nesta segunda-feira que receberá o candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, na terça-feira, quando irá declarar seu apoio ao senador para o segundo turno da eleição presidencial.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A assessoria do ex-governador de Goiás Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) informou nesta segunda-feira que receberá o candidato do PL à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro, na terça-feira, quando irá declarar seu apoio ao senador para o segundo turno da eleição presidencial. Caiado disputou o primeiro turno, ficando em quinto lugar, com 2,18% dos votos válidos. Flávio venceu o primeiro turno com 47,03% dos votos válidos. Ele enfrentará no segundo turno o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que no domingo teve 45,16% dos votos válidos. Nesta segunda-feira, o ex-governador de Minas Gerais Romeu Zema anunciou seu apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno. Zema, que disputou a Presidência pelo Novo, conquistou apenas 0,27% dos votos válidos no domingo, ficando em sexto lugar. "Nós ainda temos uma grande batalha agora dia 25, derrotar o Lula e o PT. Eu não vou me omitir nem ficar em cima do muro neste momento tão importante. Voto contra o PT, voto no Flávio Bolsonaro. O Brasil não aguenta mais quatro anos de Lula", disse Zema em vídeo divulgado no Instagram.

item.title: Diocese católica entra com ação contra governo dos EUA para garantir acesso do clero a detidos
item.description: A Arquidiocese Católica de St. Louis entrou com uma ação judicial contra o governo federal nesta segunda-feira, alegando que os detidos em um centro de detenção de imigrantes no Missouri estão sendo privados do direito de conversar em particular com padres ou de receber sacramentos como a comunhão e a confissão.
item.dc:creator: Julio-Cesar Chavez
item.content:encoded: A Arquidiocese Católica de St. Louis entrou com uma ação judicial contra o governo federal nesta segunda-feira, alegando que os detidos em um centro de detenção de imigrantes no Missouri estão sendo privados do direito de conversar em particular com padres ou de receber sacramentos como a comunhão e a confissão. A ação, movida no tribunal federal para o Distrito Leste do Missouri contra altos funcionários do Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS) e o xerife local, alega que o clero só pode visitar os detidos na Cadeia do Condado de Saint Genevieve durante um intervalo de quatro horas às segundas-feiras e só pode falar com eles por meio de um aparelho telefônico através de uma divisória de vidro. Em seu site, o Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega (ICE) afirma que os clérigos podem visitar os detidos a qualquer momento, desde que notifiquem o gabinete do xerife. A ação alega que o ICE não está cumprindo sua própria política. “Como bispo, sou responsável por cada alma em minha arquidiocese, e isso inclui aqueles que estão nas prisões”, disse o arcebispo de St. Louis, Mitchell Rozanski, à Reuters. A maioria dos cerca de 150 detidos por questões de imigração mantidos na instalação são católicos hispânicos, informou a diocese. Rozanski disse que a falta de privacidade impede os padres de exercerem suas funções pastorais. “Eles não podem ouvir confissões, não podem celebrar a missa, não podem conceder a unção dos enfermos a nenhum dos detidos”, disse ele, o que, na prática, “priva os detidos de seus direitos de ter acesso a esses sacramentos”. O ICE, o DHS, a Cadeia do Condado de Saint Genevieve e o gabinete do xerife do condado não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. Os detidos fazem parte de uma ampla campanha de repressão à imigração e deportação promovida pelo governo Trump, que tem sido condenada por grupos de direitos humanos que alegam abusos generalizados de direitos — o que o ICE nega. A lei católica não permite que os padres ouçam confissões por meios eletrônicos. Além disso, o uso de linhas não privadas nos telefones da prisão também violaria o sigilo da confissão, uma ofensa passível de excomunhão. Quando os padres solicitaram permissão para ver os detidos a fim de lhes dar a comunhão, a prisão propôs que os padres colocassem as hóstias consagradas em um recipiente e que um guarda entregasse o recipiente ao detido — uma proposta que Rozanski chamou de “sacrílega”. A Eucaristia, que os católicos acreditam conter a presença real de Deus, deve ser manuseada apenas por padres ou ministros ordenados. Em sua ação judicial, a arquidiocese solicita que os padres e outros membros do clero tenham o mesmo nível de acesso concedido a funcionários consulares e advogados ao visitarem a prisão.

item.title: Reino Unido vai monitorar continuamente dispositivos médicos baseados em IA
item.description: Os dispositivos médicos baseados em IA precisarão de monitoramento constante mesmo após serem aprovados para uso, em vez de uma única verificação de segurança prévia à aprovação, afirmou na terça-feira (horário local) o chefe do órgão regulador de medicamentos do Reino Unido.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija
item.content:encoded: Os dispositivos médicos baseados em IA precisarão de monitoramento constante mesmo após serem aprovados para uso, em vez de uma única verificação de segurança prévia à aprovação, afirmou na terça-feira (horário local) o chefe do órgão regulador de medicamentos do Reino Unido. O governo do Reino Unido aceitará todas as 44 recomendações de um relatório sobre o processo de aprovação dessas ferramentas de IA, informou. O governo se compromete a publicar um plano de implementação completo até a primavera de 2027 (no hemisfério norte), com uma versão preliminar prevista para o final deste ano. O plano definirá metas de execução e prazos para a implementação de cada mudança em todo o Serviço Nacional de Saúde (NHS). O Reino Unido é o primeiro país a desenvolver regras abrangentes para essa tecnologia emergente. Lawrence Tallon, diretor-executivo da Agência Reguladora de Medicamentos e Produtos de Saúde (MHRA, na sigla em inglês), disse à Reuters que muitos países estão agora entrando em contato com o Reino Unido para aprender com sua abordagem. “Estamos entrando em uma era muito mais sofisticada e complexa da IA como dispositivo médico, na qual temos algoritmos não determinísticos”, disse ele, referindo-se aos sistemas de IA que evoluem e se adaptam enquanto os médicos os utilizam. A MHRA também começará a aceitar inscrições para a terceira fase de seu programa “AI Airlock”, com foco na vigilância pós-comercialização e no monitoramento dos dispositivos ao longo de seu ciclo de vida depois que eles passarem a ser usados na prática clínica.

item.title: LIV Golf secures funding from BC Partners Credit to support restructuring
item.description: BC Partners Credit said on Monday it had made an initial committed investment in LIV Golf and planned to provide up to $300 million in financing to help the professional men's golf league emerge from restructuring and strengthen its financial footing ahead of the 2027 season.
item.dc:creator: Mrinmay Dey, Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: BC Partners Credit said on Monday it had made an initial committed investment in LIV Golf and planned to provide up to $300 million in financing to help the professional men's golf league emerge from restructuring and strengthen its financial footing ahead of the 2027 season. LIV Golf filed for [USN:L4N4501MD TEXT:"Chapter 11 protection"] in New Jersey in September, beginning a court-supervised restructuring process the company hopes to complete in early 2027. "Our goal is to facilitate LIV Golf's emergence from the restructuring process on sound financial footing and with renewed momentum heading into the 2027 season," Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, said in a statement. BC Partners Credit, which provides financing to middle-market companies, said the funding would support what it described as the next phase of LIV Golf, under which players would become equity owners of both the league and its teams. The financing remains subject to bankruptcy court approval and customary conditions. “This investment is an important step forward for LIV Golf, and I want to thank Ted Goldthorpe and the entire BC Partners team for their conviction in what we’re building," LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil said in a statement. "We believe deeply in the future of this league and in the opportunity to build something distinctive alongside our players," he said. "We’re delivering on our major milestones, and while there is still work ahead, today marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league that complements the wider game and creates new opportunities for players, fans, partners, and the next generation of golfers.” LIV Golf launched in 2022 with funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and lured leading players from the PGA Tour with lucrative contracts. The Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection filing, which came less than five years after it held its first event and created a schism in professional golf, revealed estimated assets of between $100 million and $500 million, with liabilities of between $500 million and $1 billion. It also listed several star golfers , including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Cameron Smith, as creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims. LIV Golf said it would continue consultations with players and other stakeholders as it works through the next steps of the process. It noted the agreement with BC Partners Credit allowed for additional time to discuss players' future participation in the league, the planned 2027 schedule and possible changes to the competitive format.

item.title: Cuba e EUA mantêm “canais de comunicação”, mas não há negociações, diz diplomata
item.description: Cuba e os Estados Unidos mantêm “canais de comunicação”, mas não estão envolvidos em nenhuma negociação formal, afirmou à Reuters a principal representante diplomática de Havana em Washington, enquanto o governo Trump prossegue com uma campanha de pressão contra a ilha governada pelos comunistas.
item.dc:creator: Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: Cuba e os Estados Unidos mantêm “canais de comunicação”, mas não estão envolvidos em nenhuma negociação formal, afirmou à Reuters a principal representante diplomática de Havana em Washington, enquanto o governo Trump prossegue com uma campanha de pressão contra a ilha governada pelos comunistas. Em entrevista nesta segunda-feira, Lianys Torres Rivera, encarregada de negócios da embaixada em Washington, disse que Cuba continua aberta a um diálogo “respeitoso”, mas “não é ingênua” em relação às ameaças do presidente Donald Trump e intensificou os preparativos para se defender contra qualquer ação militar dos EUA. Os contatos diplomáticos mais recentes entre os EUA e Cuba incluíram reuniões, ligações telefônicas e mensagens pelo WhatsApp, mas os dois lados não avançaram em relação a uma agenda de negociações ou ao reinício de conversações oficiais, disse ela. “O que temos com os EUA são canais de comunicação”, disse Torres Rivera. Ela se recusou a fornecer detalhes sobre o cronograma, os temas e os participantes. Sua descrição das comunicações parece ficar aquém da afirmação de Trump na ONU no mês passado de que o secretário de Estado Marco Rubio estava “em negociações avançadas” com Havana. Trump também chamou Cuba de “Estado falido” e previu que seu governo cairia. A delegação cubana saiu do salão em protesto. Um porta-voz do Departamento de Estado dos EUA disse: “Não nos surpreende que o regime cubano esteja divulgando essa propaganda. Na verdade, as negociações estão em andamento e o regime tem se mostrado, até o momento, relutante em concordar com qualquer coisa que ajude o povo cubano, o que, em última instância, ameaça seu controle total.” Trump declarou abertamente que seu objetivo é mudar fundamentalmente o governo de Cuba. Um bloqueio petrolífero imposto pelos EUA colocou o país sob forte pressão, já que ele enfrenta escassez de combustível e apagões agravados pela infraestrutura precária. Especialistas em direitos humanos da ONU condenaram o bloqueio petrolífero como uma violação do direito internacional. O ministro das Relações Exteriores de Cuba, Bruno Rodríguez, afirmou no final de junho que as negociações iniciadas anteriormente neste ano com os EUA haviam estagnado e, no início de setembro, que não havia negociações em andamento nem planejadas. “LINHA VERMELHA” DE CUBA Torres Rivera afirmou que a “linha vermelha” de Cuba continua sendo a recusa de Havana em negociar quaisquer mudanças em seu sistema político, considerando as exigências de Trump pela destituição da liderança cubana como uma violação da soberania. Ela rejeitou as alegações do governo Trump de que Cuba seria uma ameaça à segurança nacional dos EUA ou estaria interferindo nos assuntos internos do país, e afirmou que Washington estava usando tais acusações como pretexto para continuar pressionando economicamente a ilha, no que ela chamou de “punição coletiva”. Uma autoridade norte-americana, respondendo a perguntas da Reuters, reiterou a afirmação de Trump de que “não permitiremos que um refúgio para adversários estrangeiros ameace os Estados Unidos bem à nossa porta”. O governo Trump endureceu o embargo contra Cuba na semana passada, restringindo ainda mais as viagens de norte-americanos ao país e o acesso do setor privado cubano ao sistema bancário dos EUA. Essas medidas, disse Torres Rivera, contradizem a insistência dos EUA de que querem que Cuba expanda a iniciativa privada. Diante da pressão dos EUA, Cuba anunciou, em junho, reformas de livre mercado que, se implementadas integralmente, representariam a maior mudança na economia socialista da ilha desde que o ex-líder Fidel Castro assumiu o poder em 1959. Mas Washington afirma que as reformas não vão longe o suficiente e também exigiu eleições “livres e justas”. Apesar das divergências, Trump previu no final do mês passado que os EUA e Cuba “chegarão a um acordo”, acrescentando: “Não acho que precisaremos dos militares”. Mas o governo cubano continua cauteloso. “Cuba sempre se preparou para uma agressão dos EUA”, disse Torres Rivera. “E estamos aumentando nossas capacidades agora mais do que nunca… É para nos defendermos.”

item.title: 'Whalefall' director hopes survival story inspires awe of whales
item.description: Director Brian Duffield describes his new survival thriller "Whalefall", in which a teenager is swallowed by a sperm whale, as "the opposite of 'Jaws'".
item.dc:creator: Francesca Halliwell
item.content:encoded: Director Brian Duffield describes his new survival thriller "Whalefall", in which a teenager is swallowed by a sperm whale, as "the opposite of 'Jaws'". "I think in a lot of ways the whale is the hero of the movie," Duffield told Reuters at the film's London premiere on Monday, adding that whale experts had welcomed the film and hoped it would encourage audiences to learn more about the mammals. Based on Daniel Kraus' 2023 novel, "Whalefall" follows teenager Jay, played by Austin Abrams, who dives off California's Monastery Beach in search of his late father's remains. During the dive, he is swallowed by a sperm whale and must find a way to survive and escape. Hollywood star Josh Brolin, who plays Jay's father, said he hoped the film would have a very different impact from Steven Spielberg's shark blockbuster. "I hope (people) want to go home and hug their families and...realise that we have a short time here and might as well utilise it the best we can," he said. Beyond its survival story, the film explores grief and a complicated father-son relationship, themes that Brolin said partly drew him to the project. "I sobbed at the end of the book," he said. "Partially because of the father-son relationship, partially because it's truly a hero story." To bring the story to life, the filmmakers built large-scale whale interiors and exteriors, with computer-generated imagery used only to enhance the environments. "Everyone who worked on this movie said it was the hardest thing they've ever done," Duffield said, adding that even just sitting inside the whale set was an "incredibly dangerous stunt" for "Resident Evil" star Abrams. Kraus, who co-wrote the film's screenplay with Duffield, said the idea originated from a viral video of kayakers accidentally ending up inside a whale’s mouth. "Immediately, (I) had what I felt at the time was the best idea I've ever had," he said. "Could someone really be swallowed by a whale?" After consulting whale experts, he was told that, under the right circumstances, a person could be swallowed by a sperm whale. When asked whether Jay's fate could actually befall a human, Duffield joked that "a lot of things have to go very badly for you for it to happen." "But sperm whales are designed to do one thing and one thing only, which is eat giant squid. And so if you're smaller than a giant squid, you can fit down that throat," he said. "Who knows what happens next?" "Whalefall" will begin its global theatrical rollout on October 14.

item.title: Kraken to test Golden Knights after pair of 6-goal outbursts
item.description: The Vegas Golden Knights will try to complete a sweep of their two-game road trip through the Pacific Northwest when they face the high-scoring Seattle Kraken on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Vegas Golden Knights will try to complete a sweep of their two-game road trip through the Pacific Northwest when they face the high-scoring Seattle Kraken on Tuesday. Vegas opened the trip with a 3-2 victory at Vancouver on Sunday, its eighth straight regulation victory over the Canucks, the longest win streak against one team in franchise history. Fourth-line forward Marc Gatcomb scored the go-ahead goal late in the second period, and Adin Hill, making his first start in goal since April 9 last season, made it hold up with an 18-save performance. "He made some awesome big saves down the stretch there," forward Mitch Marner, who scored his first goal of the season, said. "It's nice to get a win and be back in the net with the guys," Hill, who played a key goaltending role on the team's 2023 Stanley Cup-winning team, said. "Had a fun night and keep her going." Gatcomb, who scored 11 goals in two seasons with the New York Islanders, tucked a rebound of Braeden Bowman's wraparound attempt inside the right post for his first goal with the Golden Knights, which proved to be the game-winner. "It's great," Gatcomb said. "You always want to get your first one with a new team out of the way. Ultimately, the goal is to win hockey games and to do anything you can to contribute. That's not always going to be a score, but anytime you can chip in on the scoresheet it's great." Seattle has sandwiched a pair of 6-1 victories over Calgary around a 3-1 loss at Edmonton and comes off a win over the Flames in its home opener on Sunday. Right wing Mackie Samoskevich, activated off the injured list after being sidelined with an upper-body injury, scored his first two goals with the Kraken since being acquired in a June trade with the Florida Panthers. Berkly Catton added a goal and an assist and Joey Daccord made 32 saves for Seattle. Daccord, the object of "Joe-ey, Joe-ey" chants from the home crowd, has stopped 56 of 58 shots in two starts this season. "It's the best. It's like the coolest thing ever," Daccord said. "This place was electric tonight. I think our whole team fed off the energy. ... The place was rocking, and pucks were going in." "He played very well for us," Kraken head coach Lane Lambert said of Daccord. "Certainly, at the start, I thought we gave him a couple (save) opportunities. What it did for us is allowed us to find some rhythm. He held it to zero, and we were able to capitalize on our opportunities." It marked the second time in three games that Seattle scored six goals. The Kraken did so just twice in 82 games last season while finishing 28th in the league in scoring with 224 goals (2.73 per game). "Sometimes it's hard to gauge why the puck is going in the net in some situations, but certainly I think our guys are shooting the puck well," Lambert said. "We did quite an emphasis in training camp on trying to make plays under duress and chaos, and I think that helped them as well." Seattle won three of the four games against Vegas last season, including both at Climate Pledge Arena. Three of the games were decided by one goal, with the Kraken winning one in overtime and another in a shootout. --Field Level Media

item.title: Terrion Arnold's friend and co-defendant pleads guilty
item.description: Boakai Hilton, a friend and co-defendant of Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold, pleaded guilty Monday in a Florida kidnapping and armed robbery case and agreed to testify against Arnold as part of the deal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boakai Hilton, a friend and co-defendant of Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold, pleaded guilty Monday in a Florida kidnapping and armed robbery case and agreed to testify against Arnold as part of the deal. Hilton, 24, was sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to three counts of kidnapping, three counts of robbery with a firearm, conspiracy to commit kidnapping and conspiracy to commit robbery with a firearm, according to the Hillsborough County State Attorney's Office. The agreement requires Hilton to testify truthfully in any future proceedings involving the case, including a potential trial for Arnold. Arnold, 23, faces eight felony charges stemming from a February incident in Tampa. He could receive a life sentence if convicted. Prosecutors allege that Arnold helped organize a plot targeting three men suspected of stealing more than $250,000 in cash and other valuables from an Airbnb he had rented in nearby Largo, Fla. The men were allegedly lured to a Tampa apartment, where they were beaten, robbed at gunpoint and held against their will for more than an hour. Investigators said they found no evidence connecting the alleged victims to the original theft. Arnold's attorneys have denied his involvement, asserting that there is no credible evidence linking him to the crimes. They also maintain that Arnold was not present at the apartment during the alleged attack. Two other defendants, Arianna Del Valle and Jasmine Randazzo, previously pleaded guilty in the case and are also required to testify truthfully in further proceedings. Arnold surrendered to authorities June 24 and was subsequently released on $1 million bond. The Detroit Lions released the former first-round pick later that month, but he signed with Seattle in August. The NFL placed Arnold on the commissioner's exempt list shortly afterward, preventing him from practicing or playing while the league reviews his situation. Arnold appeared remotely at a court hearing Monday. His next scheduled court date is Dec. 15. --Field Level Media

item.title: Protesters clash with police over Kosovo war crimes court law
item.description: Protesters clashed with police outside Kosovo's government and parliament buildings on Monday, calling for lawmakers to pass legislation that would limit the powers of a Kosovo war crimes court in The Hague.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Protesters clashed with police outside Kosovo's government and parliament buildings on Monday, calling for lawmakers to pass legislation that would limit the powers of a Kosovo war crimes court in The Hague. The protest came weeks after the [USN:L6N4580E5 TEXT:"court sentenced"] former President Hashim Thaci and three others to a combined 81 years in prison for war crimes. Police fired tear gas and used water cannon to disperse demonstrators who threw firecrackers and stones at officers guarding parliament and government buildings in central Pristina. At least 17 people were injured, including six police officers, police said. Three protesters were detained. Earlier in the day, lawmakers approved the first reading of amendments to a law that established the Kosovo war crimes court in The Hague. Demonstrators later blocked parliament, preventing lawmakers from leaving and demanding a second vote which is needed to pass the legislation. The clash underscores deep anger in Kosovo over the court's conviction of former fighters who are considered heroes and highlights growing divisions in parliament in one of Europe's poorest nations. The amendments to the Specialist Chambers law would cap prison sentences at 15 years, allow defendants to appeal to Kosovo's Supreme Court, permit sentences to be served in Kosovo and enable the country's president to grant amnesty to convicted individuals. The proposed changes faced skepticism from Prime Minister Albin Kurti. "We consider these moves to amend the law on the Specialist Chambers rushed and insufficiently analysed and thought through," Kurti told parliament. Despite backing the first vote, Kurti and his party declined to support the second vote on the same day for the amendments presented by Thaci's former party, the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK). Kosovo established the Specialist Chambers in The Hague in 2015 under international pressure to prosecute former ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) fighters for alleged crimes committed during and after Kosovo's 1998-99 war with Serbia. The court last month found Thaci, 58, guilty of war crimes including murder, torture and illegal detention, sentencing him to 25 years in prison for crimes committed as a senior commander of the KLA during the conflict. Thaci and the three co-defendants have appealed the verdict.

item.title: UK says it will monitor AI-based medical devices continually
item.description: AI-based medical devices will need constant monitoring even after they're approved for use, rather than a single pre-approval safety check, the head of the UK's medicines regulator said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija
item.content:encoded: AI-based medical devices will need constant monitoring even after they're approved for use, rather than a single pre-approval safety check, the head of the UK's medicines regulator said on Tuesday. The UK government will accept all 44 recommendations from a report on how such AI tools are approved, it said. The government commits to publishing a full implementation plan by spring 2027, with a draft plan expected by the end of the year The plan will spell out delivery targets and timelines for putting each change into place across the NHS Britain is the first country to develop comprehensive rules for this emerging technology Lawrence Tallon, Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency Chief Executive, told Reuters many nations are now approaching the UK to learn from its approach "We're moving into a much more sophisticated and complex era of AI as a medical device where we have non-deterministic algorithms," he said, referring to AI systems that evolve and adapt while doctors are using them The MHRA will also start accepting applications for the third phase of its AI Airlock program, focusing on post-market surveillance and lifecycle monitoring after devices enter clinical practice

item.title: Middle East war sharpens focus on ASEAN energy security plans
item.description: Southeast Asian energy ministers meeting in Manila this week face the prospect of a prolonged Middle East war that has exposed the region's vulnerabilities to imported energy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Southeast Asian energy ministers meeting in Manila this week face the prospect of a prolonged Middle East war that has exposed the region's vulnerabilities to imported energy. As the US-Israeli war against Iran drags on, there is increased urgency for ASEAN to implement its proposed energy security plans and reduce its exposure to price shocks caused by attacks on infrastructure and shipping routes in the Middle East. ASEAN imports more than half of the crude for its refineries from the Middle East at a time when global benchmark prices are around $100 a barrel. The conflict has also sharpened concerns about broader energy security risks as Chinese refiners have [USN:L4N45N0A8 TEXT:"suspended"] oil product exports for October. Against that backdrop, energy ministers meeting in Manila are expected to review regional fuel-security measures launched after emergency talks earlier this year, including efforts to put into effect coordinated emergency responses under the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Petroleum Security (APSA). Long-term initiatives, including the ASEAN Power Grid and renewable-energy deployment, are also on the agenda. “What the crisis brought was a sharper focus on resiliency,” Philippine Energy Undersecretary Felix Fuentebella told Reuters on October 1, saying energy security had moved from a technical issue to a priority for ASEAN ministers and leaders. LOWER EARNINGS The higher prices are raising the costs for the region's households and eating into the earnings of transport workers. “We hardly take anything home anymore,” said Antonio Bandin, a Manila jeepney driver who joined a protest last week over rising fuel prices. His working fuel bill has more than doubled to about 2,400 pesos ($38) per day. The ASEAN Centre for Energy warned in a policy paper that a severe disruption to Middle East supplies could place oil volumes equivalent to nearly 28% of ASEAN's final oil consumption at risk, underscoring the need for stronger regional petroleum-security arrangements. But the region's insufficient storage capacity and inventories remain obstacles to implementing APSA, Alloysius Joko Purwanto, senior energy economist at the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia, warned on Friday during a webinar hosted by the Center for Strategic and International Studies. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin has said the Philippines, which remains under a national energy emergency , is exploring regional fuel-stockpiling arrangements and could host future storage projects. But analysts cautioned that such measures are unlikely to affect the present crisis. “This is more about preparing for the next crisis. A reserve is a buffer. It is not a strategy,” Christopher Len, a senior fellow at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, said in the same webinar, referring to regional stockpiling initiatives. Ministers are also expected to discuss ways to reduce long-term dependence on imported fuels. Renewable energy, electric vehicles, and energy efficiency are expected to feature prominently. The International Energy Agency estimates Southeast Asia's energy import bill could rise from more than $80 billion in 2024 to about $245 billion by 2035 without structural change. The IEA said wider electrification, including electric vehicles and biofuels, would help curb oil demand and reduce exposure to volatile fuel imports, while cross-border links under the ASEAN Power Grid that would integrate the region's electrical network will require about $27 billion in investment by 2040. “We should actually use this shock as a lesson to reduce exposure, not only to cushion it,” Len said. ($1 = 62.7000 Philippine pesos)

item.title: Bolsonaro wins endorsements from right-wing rivals for Brazil election runoff
item.description: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro received on Monday endorsements from Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, two right-wing politicians who ran against him in Sunday's first-round vote, for the runoff against President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva later this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro received on Monday endorsements from Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, two right-wing politicians who ran against him in Sunday's first-round vote, for the runoff against President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva later this month. Caiado, a former governor of Goias state, won 2.18% of valid votes -- which exclude blank and null ballots -- on Sunday, while Zema, an ex-governor of Minas Gerais state, got 0.27% Caiado, from the PSD party, will meet with Bolsonaro on Tuesday to announce the endorsement, a statement from his press team said Zema, from the NOVO party, unveiled his endorsement on a post on his social media Among other candidates, author-psychiatrist Augusto Cury and Renan Santos, who received 2.89% and 2.24% of the vote, respectively, said they would not endorse Bolsonaro or Lula Bolsonaro exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"slight lead"] over Lula; the runoff is set for October 25

item.title: Ireland seeks to balance energy relief and restraint in another generous budget
item.description: Ireland will seek to stave off renewed protest over high energy costs with another generous annual budget package on Tuesday, while also attempting to moderate runaway spending growth, a rare conundrum in an otherwise cash-strapped Europe.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ireland will seek to stave off renewed protest over high energy costs with another generous annual budget package on Tuesday, while also attempting to moderate runaway spending growth, a rare conundrum in an otherwise cash-strapped Europe. Ireland has found itself in the [USN:L8N45O0I3 TEXT:"relatively unique position"] of being able to cut taxes, hike spending and set money aside in a new sovereign wealth fund thanks to [USN:L8N45O1E0 TEXT:"a surge"] in corporate tax mainly paid by a small number of US multinationals. Ministers have increasingly said they will focus the €8.5 billion ($9.53 billion) package on helping ease the impact of a three-year high in inflation through measures such as cuts to childcare costs, increases to welfare payments, supports for those struggling to pay energy bills and reductions in income tax. The government has [USN:L6N44O0RV TEXT:"already extended"] cuts to excise duties on fuels first introduced before a [USN:L1N40V05J TEXT:"wave of demonstrations"] blockaded motorways and oil infrastructure in April, briefly leaving about a third of Ireland's petrol stations without fuel. Organisers of those protests have said they may take to the streets again if the budget does not provide enough extra help. Public sector workers are also planning to take strike action next week if there is no progress on a new pay deal. The budget will be the first presented by Simon Harris since [USN:L8N3WU0HI TEXT:"he became"] finance minister last November and one of two he is scheduled to deliver before returning to the prime minister's office next year under the coalition's rotating leadership arrangement. Harris has made the establishment of a new [USN:L1N40J0SO TEXT:"personal savings and investment scheme"] a centrepiece of his plans, drip-feeding details for months on how he intends to encourage households that are among the highest savers in Europe to invest more. Harris and Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers have also pledged to keep increases in spending below 6% next year compared with an average of around 10% from 2022 to 2025 with the budget day package set to be [USN:S8N3YT0B0 TEXT:"less generous"] than a year ago. However Ireland's fiscal watchdog has already said it is larger than appropriate. The independent body has consistently warned of the risks of using the tax receipts paid by only a few companies to fund routine spending overruns. ($1 = 0.8921 euros)

item.title: Report: Eagles RB Tank Bigsby to IR with Saquon Barkley uncertain for Week 5
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Tank Bigsby needs core muscle surgery and will be placed on injured reserve, ESPN reported Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles running back Tank Bigsby needs core muscle surgery and will be placed on injured reserve, ESPN reported Monday. Bigsby suffered a core injury Sunday late in the Eagles' loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He will have the procedure done in Philadelphia and the team hopes he can be back in six weeks or less, according to the report. The injury to Philadelphia's No. 2 running back comes at an inopportune time, as Saquon Barkley's status is also up in the air after he left Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. Coach Nick Sirianni left open the possibility of Barkley playing Sunday when the Eagles face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. "I know he'll do everything he can do to get himself back. Obviously, he's a great player and a great teammate, and we always need him on the field," Sirianni said. Barkley was hurt on his second carry of the game early in the first quarter and was seen limping on the sideline. However, NBC Sports Philadelphia reported that Barkley was seen walking normally as he left the stadium. Will Shipley is the only healthy running back remaining on the Eagles' active roster. Dameon Pierce is one of three running backs currently on their practice squad; the former Houston Texans starter is in his first year with the organization. --Field Level Media

item.title: Russia says Ukraine hit two facilities at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
item.description: Ukrainian drones attacked two facilities at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine overnight on Monday, but there is no threat to nuclear safety, the head of Russia's state nuclear corporation said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian drones attacked two facilities at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southeastern Ukraine overnight on Monday, but there is no threat to nuclear safety, the head of Russia's state nuclear corporation said. Alexei Likhachev, director general of Rosatom, said a driver delivering food for plant employees was killed in the drone attack. According to Likhachev, a laboratory building and a radioactive waste processing plant were the targets. Ukraine has not commented on the incident. On Saturday, the plant's management said Ukrainian shelling over recent weeks had [USN:S8N42F00E TEXT:"damaged"] external power supply equipment at the plant, with electricity currently being provided by emergency diesel generators. The plant produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel cool. Russia seized the plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, in the first weeks of the war that began with Moscow's February 2022 invasion of its smaller neighbour. Moscow and Kyiv have since regularly accused each other of military action that compromises nuclear safety. The International Atomic Energy Agency, the UN's nuclear watchdog, has repeatedly acted to secure a ceasefire around the plant to have repairs carried out to lines connecting the plant to the main power grid. UN monitors are stationed at the Zaporizhzhia plant and three others operating in Ukraine. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, writing on her ministry's website, accused the West of enabling Ukrainian attacks by failing to condemn them publicly. "Kyiv's intensification of shelling the Zaporizhzhia plant has been made possible by the lack of an appropriate response to such actions from Western countries, which are effectively facilitating new attacks," Zakharova wrote. "Such an attitude towards strikes by the Ukrainian military demonstrates the true value of statements by representatives of these countries about nuclear and physical nuclear safety at various international forums."

item.title: Australian Army soldier dies and five others injured during training exercise
item.description: An Australian army soldier has died and five others have been injured during a training exercise in the Northern Territory of Australia, the Defence Department said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Australian army soldier has died and five others have been injured during a training exercise in the Northern Territory of Australia, the Defence Department said on Tuesday. The incident occurred at the Mount Bundey Training Area on October 5, the department said in a media statement on its website. Five other Australian Army soldiers were injured, it added. No further details of the incident were available. "Next of kin has been notified. Defence will provide further updates when possible," the statement said.

item.title: Trump says taxpayers will no longer pay for TV ads that praised him
item.description: President Donald Trump on Monday said taxpayers will no longer pay for television ads featuring him shortly before the November congressional elections after widespread criticism of the campaign-style spots.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Monday said taxpayers will no longer pay for television ads featuring him shortly before the November congressional elections after widespread criticism of the campaign-style spots. Ethics experts and lawmakers from both parties have criticized the three nationally broadcast ads, which celebrate a "golden age of America," and called for independent investigations. In a post on his Truth Social site on Monday, Trump said he considered the ads to be "a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A." but that they would no longer be funded by taxpayers and said either he or his MAGA PAC would fund the ads. Trump's MAGA Inc political action committee has about $400 million. A White House official who spoke on condition of anonymity told Reuters that going forward the ads would be paid for by the PAC. Lawmakers have questioned whether public funds are being used to promote Trump politically, while other critics say the spots may violate longstanding restrictions on government propaganda and political activity. Democratic lawmakers said last month that the White House transferred $20 million in Homeland Security Department funds to air the ads, including one that closely resembles a 2024 Trump campaign ad, and sought independent probes. The ads have run during football games as recently as Sunday and during other programming. The New York Times reported that Trump personally directed the White House budget director to use taxpayer money for the TV spots, citing sources. One ad features Trump declaring that "America will never be a communist country" while a chorus repeats the words "love me." Another combines images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a "golden age of America." The ads end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government. California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday called for an independent investigation, calling it a "staggering misuse of public funding and breach of public trust," after two Democratic congressmen last week urged a probe. FCC Chair Brendan Carr, a Republican named to his position by Trump, last week said the ads were appropriate and rejected a request to investigate them.

item.title: US envoy meets Sudanese army chief in Egypt
item.description: An envoy of President Donald Trump met the head of Sudan's army over the weekend in Egypt as the US and other intermediaries have sought to end a devastating war that has created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: An envoy of President Donald Trump met the head of Sudan's army over the weekend in Egypt as the US and other intermediaries have sought to end a devastating war that has created one of the world's [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"worst humanitarian crises"]. DETAILS: "We also reaffirm the United States' continued efforts, alongside our Egyptian partners and our other regional and international partners and allies, to advance a political solution to the crisis," US Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos said on X on Monday while describing his meeting with Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. The rare meeting came less than two weeks after Washington [USN:L6N45E0RI TEXT:"withheld a visa"] for the Sudanese army chief ahead of a scheduled UN appearance in a move that Sudanese and other sources said was linked to a US-backed ceasefire proposal that Khartoum has resisted. Sudan's army has been fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces since April 2023, when the two fell out over issues including how to integrate their forces in a planned transition to civilian rule. The US State Department said last month that neither the Sudanese Armed Forces, the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary nor either of their respective leaders "represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan." The war has displaced more than 14 million people and unleashed waves of ethnically-driven killings . "The United States stands ready to support all efforts leading to a comprehensive dialogue among the Sudanese political forces, leading to a preliminary road map of the future of the Sudan," Boulos said on Monday. Washington [USN:L6N45M0KU TEXT:"has accused"] the RSF of committing genocide and the army of carrying out war crimes. Both have previously denied abuses.

item.title: West Virginia commit Chris Wilson Jr. killed in shooting
item.description: West Virginia football commit Chris Wilson Jr., a four-star defensive end prospect from Indiana, was shot and killed early Monday morning in Muncie, Ind. He was 17.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: West Virginia football commit Chris Wilson Jr., a four-star defensive end prospect from Indiana, was shot and killed early Monday morning in Muncie, Ind. He was 17. Muncie police are investigating the shooting after finding Wilson inside a vehicle with multiple gunshot wounds in the 1400 block of East Cromer Avenue. According to police, emergency dispatchers received a report of gunfire at approximately 2:59 a.m. Wilson was pronounced dead at the scene. Authorities have not identified a suspect or released a possible motive. Wilson was a senior at Yorktown High School and one of Indiana's highest-rated football recruits in the Class of 2027. He committed to West Virginia in June, choosing the Mountaineers over offers from Auburn, Cincinnati, Purdue and several other Division I programs. The 235-pound edge rusher was ranked 31st at his position nationally and sixth overall in Indiana, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings. Wilson recorded 25 tackles, including four sacks, and an interception during his junior season in 2025, helping Yorktown capture a Class 4A sectional championship. He had 12 tackles and a sack through five games this season. Yorktown principal Stacey Brewer confirmed Wilson's death Monday in a message to students and families, saying his family had given the school permission to release the information. "With great sadness, I share that Chris Wilson, a senior at Yorktown High School, died tragically early this morning," Brewer wrote. "Chris was a valued member of our school, our football team, and our community. Our hearts are with his family, friends, and teammates." The school also informed families that local authorities had determined there was no ongoing threat to students or school facilities. Counselors will be available when classes resume following the school's fall break. Wilson was among the highest-ranked players in West Virginia's incoming recruiting class and was expected to join the Mountaineers next year. "The West Virginia football program is heartbroken by the news of the tragic loss of Chris Wilson Jr. this morning," coach Rich Rodriguez said Monday in a prepared statement. "We really enjoyed getting to know Chris during the recruiting process. The WVU football program sends its heartfelt thoughts and prayers to Chris' family in this difficult time." Police said the investigation remains ongoing. --Field Level Media

item.title: Operadora da Wikipedia diz que IA da OpenAI pode estar ligada à interrupção de serviços
item.description: A Fundação Wikimedia, que administra a enciclopédia online Wikipédia, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o tráfego intenso proveniente de agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI pode estar relacionado às interrupções que seu serviço de dados sofreu em maio.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: A Fundação Wikimedia, que administra a enciclopédia online Wikipédia, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o tráfego intenso proveniente de agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI pode estar relacionado às interrupções que seu serviço de dados sofreu em maio. A Wikimedia afirmou que pode confirmar “que descobrimos algumas atividades desses agentes ‘não autorizados’ da OpenAI nas plataformas da Wikimedia”, incluindo um incidente ocorrido em maio que resultou em uma “interrupção parcial” do serviço de consulta do Wikidata. A entidade afirmou que a interrupção parece ter sido desencadeada quando os agentes de IA da OpenAI acessaram milhões de páginas e realizaram centenas de milhares de consultas de dados. A Wikimedia também afirmou que a IA da OpenAI fez edições não autorizadas nos sites wiki da Wikimedia, incluindo “edições potencialmente maliciosas” em uma ferramenta de citação que, segundo a fundação, provavelmente tinham como objetivo se apropriar dela. A ferramenta de anotações Etherpad também foi afetada por atividades da IA da OpenAI. A OpenAI não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido feito pela Reuters para comentário.

item.title: Mercado financeiro argentino recupera forças com resultado eleitoral no Brasil
item.description: O mercado financeiro argentino operou com alta generalizada nesta segunda-feira após Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderar o primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais no Brasil na véspera, fator que ajudou a mobilizar liquidez na região, afirmaram operadores.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O mercado financeiro argentino operou com alta generalizada nesta segunda-feira após Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderar o primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais no Brasil na véspera, fator que ajudou a mobilizar liquidez na região, afirmaram operadores. A melhora dos preços foi registrada após quedas significativas no mercado doméstico e foi apoiada por uma demanda por ações do setor financeiro e títulos atrelados ao dólar. O principal índice da bolsa de Buenos Aires, o S&P Merval (.MERV) , fechou com alta de 3,68%, com destaque para o desempenho dos papéis dos bancos BBVA (BBARm.BA) e Macro (BMAm.BA) , com 5,63% e 5,24%, respectivamente. O índice havia caído 4,36% na semana passada. O Brasil é o principal parceiro comercial da Argentina. No domingo, Flávio -- que tem o apoio do presidente argentino Javier Milei -- ficou cerca de 2 pontos percentuais à frente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, no primeiro turno eleitoral: 47,03% contra 45,16%. “Consideramos que o resultado eleitoral de ontem (domingo) no Brasil é favorável para a Argentina. A vantagem de dois pontos de Bolsonaro o deixa à beira da vitória, e acreditamos que um real mais forte, taxas mais baixas e a presença de um aliado natural dentro do Mercosul favorecem os planos do presidente Milei”, afirmou a consultoria Max Capital. Enquanto isso, o peso argentino interbancário se valorizou muito levemente, em 0,07%, para 1.520,5 unidades por dólar na venda. Os títulos argentinos no mercado de balcão valorizaram 0,9% em média, enquanto o risco-país da Argentina caiu para 615 pontos básicos (17h no horário de Brasília), após atingir 655 pontos na sexta-feira, seu nível mais alto em 10 meses. (Reportagem de Hernán Nessi e Jorge Otaola)

item.title: Escritor e político britânico Jeffrey Archer morre aos 86 anos
item.description: Jeffrey Archer, o romancista britânico best-seller e ex-político que foi preso por mentir em um caso de difamação de grande repercussão, faleceu aos 86 anos, informou sua editora, a HarperCollins, nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jeffrey Archer, o romancista britânico best-seller e ex-político que foi preso por mentir em um caso de difamação de grande repercussão, faleceu aos 86 anos, informou sua editora, a HarperCollins, nesta segunda-feira. Archer vendeu mais de 300 milhões de exemplares em todo o mundo e era conhecido por thrillers cheios de ritmo. Entre os livros publicados em português estão "Cara ou Coroa" e "Eis aqui um homem". Seu último romance, “Adam and Eve”, deve ser publicado ainda este mês. Ele também foi um proeminente político conservador, que atuou brevemente como parlamentar antes de se tornar um alto dirigente do partido sob o governo da primeira-ministra Margaret Thatcher, em meados da década de 1980. Mas Archer sofreu uma queda muito pública quando foi condenado por perjúrio e obstrução da justiça em 2001, recebendo uma sentença de quatro anos de prisão. Kate Elton, presidente-executiva da HarperCollins no Reino Unido e editora de Archer, disse em um comunicado: “Estamos todos devastados por termos perdido um escritor que trouxe alegria a gerações de leitores — e um verdadeiro amigo.”

item.title: Next Artemis mission on track for 2027, but anything can happen, astronaut says
item.description: The next mission under NASA's Artemis moon program could still launch next summer as planned, but "anything can happen" given the remaining development work for the two lunar landers needed for the mission, one of the Artemis III astronauts told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: The next mission under NASA's Artemis moon program could still launch next summer as planned, but "anything can happen" given the remaining development work for the two lunar landers needed for the mission, one of the Artemis III astronauts told Reuters. NASA's third Artemis mission will be the first to involve the program's moon landers — SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. Unlike [USN:L1N40O056 TEXT:"Artemis II"], the spacecraft will stay in Earth's orbit to perform crewed docking demonstrations with Orion, a capsule whose job is to transfer the astronaut crew to the landers after getting them into space. "The biggest thing is having faith in the team to pull together, with the same rationale that anything can happen," Artemis III mission specialist Andre Douglas said in an interview on Monday, when asked if Artemis III is still on track for launch next year. Douglas, 40, fellow NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik and Frank Rubio, as well as Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, were tapped this year as [USN:L1N42H10R TEXT:"the crew for Artemis III"], seen as a key rehearsal before NASA attempts to put astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028 in Artemis IV. Both companies' lunar landers have had [USN:L1N42601G TEXT:"schedule"] [USN:L1N3ZY0WT TEXT:"delays"] while facing an unchecked list of complex development tasks, such as demonstrating the ability to store and delicately transfer super-cooled propellants in space and dock with another object in orbit. "Those are the major ones," Douglas said of the milestones the contractors need to achieve before the mission. While some industry sources doubt the landers will be ready in time for a 2027 mission, NASA has been [USN:L6N43M0HV TEXT:"optimistic"], with administrator Jared Isaacman citing good progress for "the parts that are in NASA's greatest control," referring to the NASA-owned Orion and its Space Launch System rocket. Starship and Blue Moon have received billions of dollars in NASA funding while their development remains privately managed, a commercial-focused contracting model that has given NASA relatively little control over the manner and speed with which the companies build their landers. "We just have to keep putting our heads down, leaning forward, and trying to meet the ideal timeline, which would be June of next year," said Douglas, who works with both SpaceX and Blue Origin on their lander development. He added that he and other NASA officials plan to meet with SpaceX and Blue Origin over the next few months to determine their spacecraft's readiness. The Artemis III mission had originally been planned as the program's first moon landing until February, when Isaacman imposed sweeping program changes that turned Artemis III into an extra practice mission. The agency is pressed to return to the moon quickly as it races China, which is targeting 2030 for its own first moon landing. Artemis III will be the first trip to space for Douglas, who spent years shadowing [USN:L1N40R17V TEXT:"the Artemis II crew"] as a backup. A systems engineering scholar and naval architect, Douglas has a background in the US Coast Guard that taught him how to be adaptable to rapid change, he said. "I learned in the military that the plan only lasts for 10 minutes," he said. "You have expectations, but then you're also ready in the background for change."

item.title: Chanel unveils tiger-print tweed and sheer skirt suits in spring/summer Paris show
item.description: Chanel showed see-through skirts and tiger-print tweed in creative director Matthieu Blazy's spring/summer 2027 collection on Monday as the Parisian fashion house rides a wave of enthusiasm that has helped drive sales even as other luxury brands struggle.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Chanel showed see-through skirts and tiger-print tweed in creative director Matthieu Blazy's spring/summer 2027 collection on Monday as the Parisian fashion house rides a wave of enthusiasm that has helped drive sales even as other luxury brands struggle. Since his first collection a year ago, Blazy's designs — injecting youthful glitter and loud colour combinations into the Parisian label's traditional tweed suits — have [USN:L6N41P0WR TEXT:"attracted"] new customers to the brand and kept Chanel stores buzzing with activity. Front-row guests including Dua Lipa, Nicole Kidman, and Pedro Pascal arrived to throngs of cameras in the vast expanse of the Grand Palais. The glass dome roof was hung with a giant moon and a flock of luminescent seagulls, while the floor was laid in a Martian orange-and-green pattern in reflective resin. Models emerged wearing skirt suits in sheer cream or black fabric embroidered with flowers and beads, and in tweed loosened into a wide windowpane print with mesh panels, or reworked in an eye-catching red-and-white tiger print. “Chanel felt as alive as ever,” said Angélique Liautaud, womenswear buying and merchandising director at French department store Printemps. “The masculine wardrobe, the fluid dresses, the lingerie, the liberated body, brought a new sensuality to the house.” Some skirts were sliced into swinging panels, others were shortened into pleated mini-skirts paired with cropped jackets showing the midriff. Hems were frayed or finished with metallic beading. Models sported new versions of the brand's two-tone pumps — in leopard print or tiger print with a cream toe, or baby blue and silver, while sandals were chunky with a large interlocking C logo in gold across the front. Quilted handbags came in black, burgundy, and white with a couple of wild variations in zebra print layered with clashing primary colours. Blazy, known for soundtracking his shows to anthems from the 2000s, ran out to greet the crowd after the finale to the heavy synths of "Gimme More" by Britney Spears.

item.title: Eagles take drop-in travel approach to London game vs. Jaguars
item.description: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wants to prepare for the Jaguars at home, delaying travel for Sunday's game in London to Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wants to prepare for the Jaguars at home, delaying travel for Sunday's game in London to Friday. The travel plan calls for a charter flight scheduled to span around seven hours from Philadelphia to England on Friday, with the Eagles returning immediately after the game Sunday. "We felt like leaving Friday was best for our team, this team, and with the schedule that we have with the weeks coming up," Sirianni said. "At the end of the day, I got to make those decisions and this is the decision I chose, with the help of great people." The wisdom in covering more than 7,000 air miles in a tight window of time -- roughly 48 hours -- is likely to be a hot topic for the Eagles. Because of the time change, the Eagles will land in London on Saturday morning. The potential for jet lag was not a deterrent for Sirianni as the Eagles (2-2) try to rebound from consecutive losses to the Bears and Rams. "We went through all of this," Sirianni said. "We feel like this is giving our team the best chance to win." --Field Level Media

item.title: Euroleague to vote on expansion offers on Tuesday as NBA Europe talks loom
item.description: Euroleague shareholder clubs are unlikely to embrace radical change when they meet this week to consider a 10-year strategic plan, experts said on Monday, in a pivotal week for the sport across the continent with the NBA looking to move in.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Euroleague shareholder clubs are unlikely to embrace radical change when they meet this week to consider a 10-year strategic plan, experts said on Monday, in a pivotal week for the sport across the continent with the NBA looking to move in. Representatives from the 13 permanent Euroleague teams were due in Lake Como on Monday night with a vote on Tuesday on a fundamental ownership shift that would transform those shareholders into franchises and expand the competition from 20 teams to 24. The Euroleague will also evaluate the 14 bids they have received for additional long-term franchise spots, with a maximum of eight to be awarded by ballot. The proposals from the Euroleague are aimed at sustainability and accelerating long-term growth but sceptics remain. "I don't think it really changes what it's on the table today for the 13 shareholders," Lega Basket Serie A President Maurizio Gherardini told Reuters. The strategic plan aims for an aggregate value of the competition and its clubs of €4.3 billion ($4,82 billion) by 2027 and said in a statement on August 25 that projected year-on-year revenue growth had risen to 15% as a result of fresh commercial deals. Despite the positive projections, Real Madrid budgets show net losses in the basketball division each year since the 2021-22 season. Counterparts Barcelona have posted overall net losses for the past three years, and economist Ivan Cabeza told Reuters that the wider Euroleague model was not sustainable. "I find it very hard to see how a business like the Euroleague which has been, is, and very likely will continue to be a money-losing venture, could undergo a radical change," Cabeza said. This could make the NBA Europe project appealing to clubs primarily focused on football, with the North American league widely expected to launch in 2027 - with or without Euroleague's cooperation. The Athletic reported last week that NBA Europe managing director George Aivazoglou and NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum held discussions with Paris St Germain, AC Milan and the Spanish duo about becoming member franchises. Media reports said the NBA have submitted a proposal to the Euroleague, which last Friday confirmed to Reuters that talks were ongoing between the two. "If someone came along and said, 'Look, I’ll give you €800 million ($896,88 million) to take over the franchise so you never lose money again', that’s obviously an attractive proposition," said Cabeza, posing a hypothetical for Barcelona and Real Madrid. "It’s appealing because it solves part of your overall debt problem, stops the financial bleeding, and allows you to keep the brand name associated with a partner." Aivazoglou is poised to give an update on their 16-team competition on Thursday in London. Both the NBA and the Euroleague have confirmed they will forge ahead with their own plans for the 2027-28 season if no agreement is found. ($1 = 0.8920 euros)

item.title: Imea mantém projeções da safra 26/27 de soja e milho de MT; vê alta na área de algodão
item.description: O Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea) manteve em outubro suas estimativas para a safra de soja e milho 2026/27 de Mato Grosso, apesar do atraso inicial da semeadura da oleaginosa provocado pela irregularidade das primeiras chuvas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea) manteve em outubro suas estimativas para a safra de soja e milho 2026/27 de Mato Grosso, apesar do atraso inicial da semeadura da oleaginosa provocado pela irregularidade das primeiras chuvas. O órgão vinculado à federação dos produtores Famato ressaltou que as condições climáticas nos próximos meses serão determinantes para confirmar o potencial produtivo da temporada. As projeções de área, produtividade e produção de soja foram mantidas em 13,05 milhões de hectares, 62,44 sacas de 60 kg por hectare e 48,88 milhões de toneladas, respectivamente. Se confirmada, a projeção de safra do principal Estado produtor brasileiro teria uma queda de cerca de 5% ante o ciclo anterior, baseada em uma produtividade mais baixa, visto que a área teria um leve crescimento. Segundo o instituto, a semeadura começou no Estado, mas segue atrasada em relação às últimas safras devido à irregularidade das precipitações e à cautela dos produtores diante do risco de interrupção das chuvas após o plantio. "Até o momento, contudo, o atraso ocorre em uma fase ainda inicial da implantação das lavouras e não apresenta magnitude suficiente para justificar alterações nas estimativas de produtividade e produção", afirmou o Imea em relatório mensal. O instituto destacou ainda que o foco do mercado passa a ser o comportamento climático entre novembro e dezembro, período crucial para o desenvolvimento das lavouras, em um ano sob influência do El Niño. "A eventual ocorrência de veranicos, sobretudo se coincidir com fases mais sensíveis da cultura, como florescimento e formação de vagens, poderá limitar o potencial produtivo", alertou. Para o milho 2026/27, cuja área plantada pode sofrer influência do ritmo de plantio da soja e da definição da janela ideal de plantio da segunda safra, o Imea também manteve suas projeções. A área destinada ao cereal permaneceu estimada em 7,48 milhões de hectares, avanço de 0,59% ante a temporada 2025/26. A produtividade foi mantida em 119,64 sacas por hectare, queda de 8,05% na comparação anual, enquanto a produção seguiu projetada em 53,68 milhões de toneladas, recuo de 7,50%. O instituto afirmou que a demanda doméstica aquecida continua sustentando a atratividade econômica da cultura no Estado. ALGODÃO Em sua primeira estimativa para a safra de algodão 2026/27, o Imea projetou aumento de 3,8% da área cultivada em Mato Grosso, para 1,43 milhão de hectares, impulsionado pelos preços mais atrativos da pluma. "O momento atual de preços mais atrativos da pluma tem motivado o investimento na cultura para a próxima temporada", afirmou o instituto. A produção, entretanto, poderia recuar 2,4% ante o ciclo anterior, para 2,73 milhões de toneladas da pluma, uma vez que o Imea vê produtividades mais baixas. O instituto ponderou, porém, que as projeções ainda estão sujeitas às condições climáticas da temporada, incluindo possíveis efeitos do fenômeno El Niño e eventuais atrasos na colheita da soja, que podem postergar a semeadura do algodão de segunda safra e elevar a exposição da cultura ao risco climático.

item.title: New Zealand third quarter business confidence jumps, says think tank
item.description: New Zealand's business confidence rose in the third quarter even as fuel prices increased and geopolitics remained a headwind for the country, a private think tank said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand's business confidence rose in the third quarter even as fuel prices increased and geopolitics remained a headwind for the country, a private think tank said on Tuesday. A net 43% of firms surveyed expected general business conditions to improve compared with 8% optimism in the previous quarter, the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research's quarterly survey of business opinion showed. The survey was undertaken from September 9 to 28 and coincided with a surge in fuel prices amid a reescalation of the conflict between the US and Iran. “These recent developments highlight ongoing volatility and uncertainty in global oil supply and prices, but the impact on sentiment appears muted for now,” NZIER said in a statement. On a seasonally adjusted basis, 40% expected business conditions to improve versus 14% optimism recorded in the previous period. The survey's measure of capacity utilization rose to 91.0%, from the previous quarter's 90.8%. “There is once again that divergence between what firms experience, which is still fairly weak activity, and what they’re expecting for the next quarter, which generally is one of an improvement ahead,” Christina Leung, principal economist at NZIER, said at a press conference. NZIER said in a statement that the stabilisation in costs and pricing indicators in the latest survey suggests a modest risk of higher fuel prices flowing through to broader inflation pressures. Leung said NZIER does not believe there needs to be any further cash rate hikes this year. New Zealand’s central bank increased the cash rate by 25 basis points in [USN:L1N44U036 TEXT:"September"] to 2.75% and signaled more tightening ahead, but stressed any further moves would be measured as it warned of mounting risks to the economic outlook.

item.title: L'Oreal explores unloading chemical-related liabilities, WSJ reports
item.description: L'Oreal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Oreal (OREP.PA) has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. The cosmetics maker's US unit is working with restructuring counsel Weil Gotshal & Manges and investment bank Ducera Partners to address lawsuits from individuals alleging the talc products caused illness, the Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter. L'Oreal said in its latest half-year report that about 760 US proceedings over the alleged presence of asbestos particles in some talc-containing cosmetic products were pending as of June 30, up from about 620 at the end of 2025, and that it strongly contests the claims. The Journal said L'Oreal is considering moving tort liabilities into a separate corporate entity to unload them through a sale to an outside investor, allowing the company to separate its exposure from its operating businesses. As an option to address the claims outside Chapter 11, L'Oreal's advisers are exploring a sale similar to Honeywell's (HON.O) [USN:L3N3VI1RX TEXT:"divestiture"] last year of certain asbestos liabilities to corporate liability acquisition platform Delticus, the Journal said. L'Oreal, Weil Gotshal & Manges and Ducera did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. More broadly, talc litigation has cost Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) billions of dollars in a legal fight lasting more than a decade, and has prompted several companies to try to resolve claims in bankruptcy court. In July, J&J said it would pay an estimated [USN:L1N43U01Q TEXT:"$5.5 billion"] to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its baby powder and other talc products cause ovarian cancer. It had earlier filed for three bankruptcies through a shell-company subsidiary in an effort to settle the cases, though each ended in dismissal. Avon Products, a US-based holding company of the Avon beauty brand, started Chapter 11 proceedings in 2024 to address its debt and talc liabilities. L'Oreal is also facing thousands of lawsuits alleging its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women. Arizona [USN:L6N45313S TEXT:"sued"] L'Oreal and its US subsidiary in September, alleging the cosmetics company hid evidence that the products could cause cancer. L'Oreal USA has previously said the company is confident in the safety of its products and believes those claims are without legal or scientific merit.

item.title: Trading Day: Nasdaq highs, Brazil surprise
item.description: The Nasdaq surged to a fresh high on Monday, as earnings optimism and lower oil prices offset rising bond yields. The biggest moves of the day were in Brazilian assets, which logged historic gains after right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro's strong showing in the first round of voting in the presidential election suggests he is a strong favorite to win the second and decisive round in three weeks.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
The [USN:L6N45R0IS TEXT:"Nasdaq"] surged to a fresh high on Monday, as earnings optimism and [USN:L4N45Q02S TEXT:"lower oil"] prices offset rising bond yields. The biggest moves of the day were in [USN:L1N45R0C7 TEXT:"Brazilian assets"], which logged historic gains after right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro's strong showing in the first round of voting in the presidential election suggests he is a strong favorite to win the second and decisive round in three weeks. In [USN:L6N45O107 TEXT:"my column today"], I look at when traders and financial TV anchors on the NYSE floor should start ordering their "S&P 10,000" caps. That milestone is only 30% from current levels, and if Q3 earnings are anywhere near as strong as Q2, it suddenly won't feel too far away at all. Today's Talking Points: Brazil That rumbling you feel beneath your feet is the first tremors of what could be a political earthquake in Brazil. Right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former hard-right President [USN:S0N42U07U TEXT:"Jair"] Bolsonaro, did much better than expected in the first round of voting in Sunday's presidential election, and from a financial markets viewpoint at least, the [USN:L1N45R09E TEXT:"verdict"] is clear — the sizzling rally in Brazilian assets on Monday says it all. Incumbent [USN:L1N45R0KI TEXT:"Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva"], the left-wing veteran going for his fourth non-consecutive term, is considering tapping Vice President Geraldo Alckmin to be his next finance minister if re-elected, in a bid to bolster his fiscal credibility and win over centrist voters. But it may be too little too late — online betting markets are pointing to an 83% likelihood that Bolsonaro wins in the second round of voting. Europe To France, Italy and Germany last week, investors can add Spain to their European political risk watch-list, after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election following nationwide protests over housing. It's a high-stakes gamble for Sanchez, whose Socialist Party trails in nearly every opinion poll. Defeat would spell the end of one of Europe's last remaining left-leaning governments at a time when the far right is making unprecedented gains across the region. Spain's political turmoil isn't tied to fiscal concerns like other countries — Spain is one of the fastest-growing economies in the euro zone, its deficit is around 2-2.5% of GDP, and yield spreads are under relative control. Still, markets are twitchy — Spanish yields rose 5 bps and the euro slumped to a fresh 17-month low around $1.12. Dollar In G10 FX, the big beneficiary of deepening political and bond market uncertainty sweeping, to varying degrees, across Europe, the UK and Japan is the dollar. The US doesn't have its political, debt or bond market troubles to seek either, of course. But to coin an old FX market adage, the greenback is once again proving to be the cleanest dirty shirt in the laundry. This isn't what President Trump or Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent really want. They would prefer a weaker dollar that is more competitive in the global marketplace, which would theoretically help boost US exports and narrow the trade deficit that Trump says is a result of America being "ripped off" by the rest of the world. On the other hand, a stronger dollar helps suppress imported price pressures and the need for tighter monetary policy. Now that's music to Trump's ears. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (adductor) day-to-day, could play Week 5
item.description: While Ja'Marr Chase is in the league's concussion protocol, his longtime receiving mate in Cincinnati, Tee Higgins, may not have to miss game action following his adductor injury Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: While Ja'Marr Chase is in the league's concussion protocol, his longtime receiving mate in Cincinnati, Tee Higgins, may not have to miss game action following his adductor injury Sunday. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Higgins is day-to-day, and he didn't rule out the possibility that Higgins could play Week 5 at the Miami Dolphins. "(We'll) see where he is at this week," Taylor told reporters. Higgins injured his adductor following a toe-tapping sideline grab late in Cincinnati's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He left briefly and returned for one play on the Bengals' final drive but was unable to continue. Higgins reeled in 11 receptions for 157 yards. The 27-year-old has 25 receptions for 401 yards and one touchdown in four games this season for Cincinnati (2-2). His production Sunday was critical after Chase, 26, was ruled out with a concussion after his head hit the turf early in the second quarter. Chase, 26, has 21 receptions for 212 yards and three touchdowns over four games this season. In six NFL seasons, all with the Bengals, the five-time Pro Bowl selection has 541 receptions for 7,049 yards and 57 touchdowns. In his seventh season in Cincinnati, Higgins has 414 catches for 5,842 yards and 46 touchdowns. He earned his first Pro Bowl selection last year, posting a career-high 11 touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cuba y EEUU mantienen "canales de comunicación", pero no hay negociaciones: diplomática
item.description: Cuba y Estados Unidos han mantenido "canales de comunicación", pero no hay una negociación formal, dijo a Reuters la máxima representante diplomática de La Habana en Washington, mientras el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump prosigue con su campaña de presión contra la isla gobernada por el régimen comunista.
item.dc:creator: Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: Cuba y Estados Unidos han mantenido "canales de comunicación", pero no hay una negociación formal, dijo a Reuters la máxima representante diplomática de La Habana en Washington, mientras el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump prosigue con su campaña de presión contra la isla gobernada por el régimen comunista. En una entrevista concedida el lunes, Lianys Torres Rivera, encargada de negocios de la embajada en Washington, dijo que Cuba sigue abierta a un diálogo "respetuoso", pero que "no es ingenua" respecto a las amenazas del presidente Donald Trump y ha intensificado los preparativos para defenderse de cualquier acción militar estadounidense. Los últimos contactos diplomáticos entre Estados Unidos y Cuba han consistido en reuniones, así como en llamadas telefónicas y mensajes de WhatsApp, pero ninguna de las dos partes ha avanzado hacia una agenda de negociación ni hacia la reanudación de las conversaciones oficiales, señaló. "Lo que tenemos con Estados Unidos son canales de comunicación", dijo Torres Rivera, que no quiso dar detalles sobre los plazos, los temas y los participantes. Su descripción de las comunicaciones parece distar de la afirmación de Trump el mes pasado ante las Naciones Unidas de que el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se encontraba "en plenas negociaciones" con La Habana. Trump también calificó a Cuba de "Estado fallido" y predijo que su Gobierno caería. La delegación cubana abandonó la sala en señal de protesta.
