Trump ha declarado abiertamente que su objetivo es cambiar de forma radical el Gobierno de Cuba. En respuesta a las preguntas de Reuters, un funcionario estadounidense no dio detalles sobre los contactos diplomáticos, pero dijo, bajo condición de anonimato: "Estados Unidos está dispuesto a abrir un nuevo capítulo en la relación (…) Lo único que se interpone en el camino hacia un futuro mejor son aquellos que controlan Cuba para su propio beneficio a costa del pueblo cubano". Torres Rivera dijo que la "línea roja" de Cuba sigue siendo que La Habana no está dispuesta a negociar ningún cambio en su sistema político, y considera que las exigencias de Trump de que se destituya a los dirigentes cubanos constituyen una violación de la soberanía.

item.title: France come from behind to thrash Belgium 4-1
item.description: France came from a goal down to beat Belgium 4-1 in their Nations League Group A1 meeting at the Stade de France on Monday, while Italy secured a 3-1 win over Turkey, their third consecutive match without a loss.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France came from a goal down to beat Belgium 4-1 in their Nations League Group A1 meeting at the Stade de France on Monday, while Italy secured a 3-1 win over Turkey, their third consecutive match without a loss. Zinedine Zidane secured his first home win in charge, three days after a 1-1 draw against Italy, thanks to his substitutes. Belgium's Dodi Lukebakio put the visitors ahead in the 35th minute, but Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki and Michael Olise, all on the bench at kickoff, turned the match on its head in the final 15 minutes. Doue levelled with a left-footed shot from the edge of the box in the 77th minute. Four minutes later, Cherki put his side in front, finishing from an Olise cross. Olise then completed a brace from close range just before and during stoppage time. "That's football, that's what we love. There were difficulties, but that's part of the game, part of the kinds of matches you can have," Zidane told TF1. "It's good to put things right, and that's what we did with an extraordinary second half. We were just missing that final few metres in the first half, but then we turned the match around, it was good." Belgium took the lead when Lukebakio broke clear of a defence that was stepping up for offside to latch onto a long pass from Romeo Lavia, before scoring in a one-on-one with Guillaume Restes, who was earning his first cap. The 2018 World Cup winners, playing without captain Kylian Mbappe, controlled possession but failed to create chances against a packed defensive block, making it an eighth consecutive match without scoring in the first half. Then Olise and Cherki came off the bench on the hour mark, 12 minutes before Doue, and France became more dangerous. "We played well at the end; in the first half it was difficult against their low block. After that we kept going and it was good in the end," Olise told TF1. "It's a team effort, Zidane brings ideas and we follow them. We're going to keep going like this." After Maarten Vandevoordt, who was also winning his first cap, denied efforts from Bradley Barcola, Esteban Lepaul, Olise and Cherki, the Belgian goalkeeper was unable to stop Doue's strike. The Paris St Germain winger levelled with a left-footed shot across goal from the edge of the box. Four minutes later, Olise began his masterclass. He first delivered a cross for Cherki to score before completing a quickfire double from close range within three minutes to give France a resounding victory. Italy's victory over Turkey came with Gianluca Scamacca, Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito scoring, while Aral Simsir had earlier equalised just after the hour mark. Scamacca scored the opener with a close‑range volley that hit the crossbar before crossing the line. Simsir levelled at the far post at the end of a beautiful team move from the Turks, but three minutes later Calafiori's header from a Nicolo Barella free kick restored Italy's lead. Esposito scored the final goal after Issa Doumbia and Alessandro Romano had both failed to convert. "Even though we had made a lot of changes, there was fatigue all around, and we struggled a bit," coach Roberto Mancini told RAI. "But we did well to score, and then to score again right after they equalised." France sit top with 10 points, three ahead of Italy and four clear of Belgium. Turkey are bottom with four defeats from four matches.

item.title: Ravens optimistic QB Lamar Jackson ankle injury isn't 'crazy long-term'
item.description: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is not ruled out for Week 5, a Sunday night matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, but Baltimore is bracing for his absence to stretch beyond the second half of a Week 4 win.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is not ruled out for Week 5, a Sunday night matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, but Baltimore is bracing for his absence to stretch beyond the second half of a Week 4 win. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said it's too early to know what Jackson's status could be for this week. Jackson injured his left ankle and wore a protective boot out of the stadium on Sunday night after sitting out the second half of a 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long-term, but we'll see what happens," Minter said. The Ravens (3-1) share the AFC North lead with the Cleveland Browns (3-1), who will host Baltimore on Oct. 18. Jackson's status won't be updated until Wednesday afternoon, Minter said. The Ravens would start Tyler Huntley against the Falcons if Jackson isn't available. Huntley completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards in the second half to steer Baltimore past Tennessee. Minter said Monday he didn't "know the chances yet" that Huntley could be in line to make his 12th start with the Ravens. He's 5-6 as a spot starter with Baltimore. "We're still gathering a lot of the information and the imaging and things like that, just dealing with a little bit of an ankle and we'll kind of see where that shakes out," Minter said of Jackson's status. "Full trust and confidence in him that when it's ready to roll that we'll roll and go from there." --Field Level Media

item.title: Jeffrey Archer, bestselling UK novelist and scandal-plagued politician, dies aged 86
item.description: Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling British novelist and former politician who was jailed for lying in a high-profile libel case, has died aged 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jeffrey Archer, the bestselling British novelist and former politician who was jailed for lying in a high-profile libel case, has died aged 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday. Archer sold over 300 million copies worldwide and was known for pacy thrillers like his 1976 debut "Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less" and 1979's "Kane & Abel". His final novel, "Adam and Eve", is due to be published on Tuesday. Kate Elton, HarperCollins' UK CEO and Archer's editor, said in a statement: "We're all devastated to have lost a writer who has brought joy to generations of readers — and a true friend." Archer was also a prominent Conservative politician, who briefly served as a lawmaker before becoming a senior party official under then-Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the mid-1980s. But he was as well-known for his very public downfall. In 1987, Archer sued the Daily Star tabloid for saying he had paid a woman for sex, winning a then-record £500,000 ($660,450) in damages. The case returned to the public eye when he was selected as the Conservative candidate to become London's first elected mayor in 1999. A former friend accused him of lying and Archer was eventually charged with perjury and perverting the course of justice, convicted and sentenced to four years' imprisonment. He served two years, during which time he wrote "A Prison Diary". ARCHER TRIAL NOTORIOUS FOR JUDGE'S SUMMING UP The trial of Archer's libel case, which was heard in front of a jury, became notorious for the judge's summing up of evidence given by Archer's wife Mary. "Remember Mary Archer in the witness box," the judge, Bernard Caulfield, told the jury. "Your vision of her will probably never disappear. Has she elegance? Has she fragrance? Would she have, without the strain of this trial, radiance?" And, of Archer, he added: "Is he in need of cold, unloving, rubber-insulated sex in a seedy hotel?" Archer's reputation as one of the most colourful figures in British public life did no harm to his literary career. His books were sold in 119 countries, HarperCollins said. He spent a total of five-and-a-half years on the New York Times bestseller lists. He was due to speak about his final novel this weekend at the Cheltenham Literature Festival and had recently appeared on radio shows to promote the book. HarperCollins said he had died suddenly and peacefully, "between writing sessions". ($1 = 0.7571 pounds)

item.title: Nova York declara estado de emergência devido a surto de sarampo
item.description: A governadora de Nova York, Kathy Hochul, declarou nesta segunda-feira estado de emergência em todo o Estado devido a um surto de sarampo, a primeira declaração do tipo feita por um Estado norte-americano desde que os casos começaram a aumentar, em 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A governadora de Nova York, Kathy Hochul, declarou nesta segunda-feira estado de emergência em todo o Estado devido a um surto de sarampo, a primeira declaração do tipo feita por um Estado norte-americano desde que os casos começaram a aumentar, em 2025. O Estado também ampliou o número de profissionais de saúde autorizados a administrar vacinas contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola devido ao aumento de casos em comunidades rurais. Nova York registrou 108 casos de sarampo neste ano até 3 de outubro -- 92 deles de 15 de julho ao início de outubro -- em comunidades rurais com baixa cobertura vacinal em 18 condados, bem acima dos níveis anuais típicos, de acordo com o decreto da governadora. O Estado vizinho da Pensilvânia está enfrentando um surto de rápida propagação, com 977 casos e cinco mortes até 2 de outubro, principalmente em condados rurais que fazem fronteira com Nova York, segundo o decreto. O decreto permite que enfermeiros registrados solicitem exames para suspeita de sarampo e que farmacêuticos vacinem crianças a partir de dois anos de idade. Também exige que todas as vacinações contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola sejam registradas nos sistemas de imunização estaduais ou da cidade de Nova York em até 72 horas, dispensando o consentimento de adultos para tal comunicação. A vacinação em si ainda requer o consentimento do paciente ou de um responsável legal. O estado de emergência entrou em vigor nesta segunda-feira e vai até 4 de novembro.

item.title: Dezenas de pessoas estão em quarentena na Sibéria após morte de funcionária de laboratório de instituto sobre peste
item.description: Uma funcionária de laboratório de um instituto de pesquisa sobre a peste na Sibéria adoeceu e faleceu em circunstâncias não reveladas, levando as autoridades a colocarem dezenas de pessoas em quarentena e fazendo com que a chefe do órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia se deslocasse à região de Irkutsk.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn
item.content:encoded: Uma funcionária de laboratório de um instituto de pesquisa sobre a peste na Sibéria adoeceu e faleceu em circunstâncias não reveladas, levando as autoridades a colocarem dezenas de pessoas em quarentena e fazendo com que a chefe do órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia se deslocasse à região de Irkutsk. A morte gerou temores relacionados à saúde pública nas redes sociais, mas as autoridades afirmaram nesta segunda-feira que a situação estava sob controle. A Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) afirmou que, com base nas informações disponíveis, “o risco à saúde pública para a população em geral parece ser baixo”. Novas avaliações de risco serão realizadas assim que mais informações forem divulgadas, informou a organização. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, disse que a morte era um “grande problema para a Rússia” e se ofereceu para ajudar Moscou a lidar com a situação. “Vamos ajudar”, disse Trump. “Para quem tiver esse tipo de problema, estamos sempre dispostos a ajudar.” O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, disse que Washington estava acompanhando de perto a situação. A peste é endêmica na Sibéria, local do primeiro surto humano pré-histórico conhecido, já que a bactéria que a causa, a Yersinia pestis, está presente entre os pequenos mamíferos selvagens em suas vastas áreas e em suas pulgas. É raro que russos adoeçam com a peste, no entanto, embora casos em outras partes do mundo — notadamente na África — ocorram todos os anos. A peste se apresenta em três formas que afetam diferentes partes do corpo. A peste pneumônica, uma infecção dos pulmões, faz com que o paciente espalhe gotículas infecciosas pelo ar ao tossir. Se diagnosticada rapidamente, pode ser tratada com antibióticos. Mas, se não for tratada, pode ser fatal em um a seis dias. A mídia local identificou a mulher como Darya Shipilova, funcionária do Instituto de Pesquisa Antipeste de Irkutsk da Sibéria e do Extremo Oriente. Houve relatos contraditórios sobre como e onde a funcionária do laboratório, cuja idade foi informada como 28 anos, havia adoecido, mas as autoridades afirmaram que ela havia morrido de pneumonia de origem ainda não determinada. AUTORIDADES DIZEM QUE NÃO FORAM RELATADOS NOVOS CASOS E QUE TODOS OS CONTATOS FORAM RASTREADOS O órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia, Rospotrebnadzor, informou à mídia estatal que o instituto não havia encontrado evidências de nenhum acidente envolvendo o manuseio de patógenos, após rumores se espalharem nas redes sociais de que a mulher teria deixado cair um tubo de ensaio contendo bactérias vivas. No entanto, Anna Popova, chefe da Rospotrebnadzor, voou para a Sibéria para uma reunião de emergência no fim de semana. De acordo com reportagens da mídia russa, cerca de 200 pessoas que tiveram contato com a mulher falecida foram colocadas em quarentena, partes do hospital na cidade de Shelekhov, onde ela faleceu, foram isoladas e uma fábrica de alumínio orientou seus funcionários a usarem máscaras. A Rospotrebnadzor, em comunicado posterior citado pela agência de notícias Tass, informou que autoridades da região de Irkutsk haviam identificado dois casos de Covid e dois casos de rinovírus entre as pessoas que estiveram em contato com ela. Nenhum outro caso de doenças infecciosas foi registrado. As autoridades pediram que as pessoas mantivessem a calma e afirmaram que não havia evidências de que a morte da mulher estivesse relacionada ao seu trabalho. Igor Kobzev, governador da região de Irkutsk, afirmou em comunicado que ela havia falecido de “pneumonia de etiologia desconhecida”, acrescentando: “É importante ressaltar que, nos últimos dias, não foram identificados novos casos de funcionários do Instituto Antipeste que procurassem atendimento médico.” Ele afirmou que a situação estava sob controle e que todos os contatos conhecidos da mulher falecida haviam sido identificados, examinados e colocados sob supervisão médica.

item.title: Data centre operator DayOne reveals revenue surge in US IPO filing
item.description: Data center operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-center listings amid challenging market conditions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Data center operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-center listings amid challenging market conditions. The company posted a net loss of $77.2 million on revenue of $512 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a loss of $12.6 million on revenue of $151.5 million a year earlier. The filing comes as surging bond yields and elevated interest rates cloud the outlook for the fall IPO market, prompting several major listings to be [USN:L6N45L0OG TEXT:"postponed"]. Data centers have also come under scrutiny over their heavy use of electricity, water and land, with communities raising concerns about their impact on power grids, utility bills and local resources. The Singapore-based company develops and operates data centers for cloud-computing and AI customers, providing space, power, cooling and connectivity, primarily under long-term contracts. DayOne operates across Asia-Pacific and Europe, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain, according to its filing. Shanghai-based GDS Holdings set up GDS International in Singapore in 2022, which was rebranded as DayOne in January 2025 following its separation from the parent company. The company has not disclosed the size of the offering, although Reuters [USN:L4N3Z90C5 TEXT:"reported"] in February that it was aiming to raise as much as $5 billion at a potential valuation of $20 billion. DayOne plans to use the IPO proceeds to develop and construct new data-center projects and for working capital and other general corporate purposes. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities and Citigroup are among the underwriters for the offering. DayOne plans to list its American depositary shares on the Nasdaq under the symbol “DODC.”

item.title: Centalion acquires Haynesville natural gas assets from Silver Hill
item.description: Centalion Group said on Monday it acquired upstream and midstream natural gas assets in Texas and Louisiana's Haynesville region from Texas-based private shale company Silver Hill Energy Partners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Centalion Group said on Monday it acquired upstream and midstream natural gas assets in Texas and Louisiana's Haynesville region from Texas-based private shale company Silver Hill Energy Partners. The commodities trader, formerly known as Gunvor, [USN:L1N45O096 TEXT:"rebranded"] as Centalion Group last week and said it planned to redomicile its corporate headquarters to Singapore from Cyprus. A Centalion spokesperson said the company's Haynesville platform, comprising the Post Oak and Silver Hill assets, has an enterprise value of about $2 billion. Reuters [USN:L1N44M0TQ TEXT:"reported"] in August that Centalion was in talks to acquire the Silver Hill assets in a deal valued at between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion, citing sources familiar with the matter. The assets have current net natural gas production of about 300 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd) and the portfolio includes about 72,000 net acres in the Haynesville and Bossier development areas. "The rationale is for us to have a footprint in a basin that is the pivot point between domestic and export markets, allowing us to capture and create value from that optionality," the spokesperson added.

item.title: New York declares first US measles disaster emergency since 2025 surge
item.description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a U.S. state since cases began surging in 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration by a U.S. state since cases began surging in 2025. The state also expanded the pool of health professionals allowed to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines as cases rise in rural communities. "No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease," Hochul said in a statement. New York has reported 108 measles cases this year through October 3, including 92 since July 15 in under-immunized rural communities across 18 counties, well above typical annual levels, according to the executive order. Seven of the cases are in New York City and 101 are elsewhere in the state, the governor's office said. Local health departments have administered more than 1,000 MMR doses in rural areas since July 15. Neighboring Pennsylvania is battling a fast-spreading outbreak, with 977 cases and five deaths as of October 2, mostly in rural counties that border New York, the order said. Pennsylvania health officials said on Monday the state's total had passed 1,000 cases, making it the largest state outbreak in more than three decades. The US is having its worst year for measles since 1991, with nearly 3,900 cases reported, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The order allows registered nurses to order tests for suspected measles and pharmacists to vaccinate children as young as two. It also requires all MMR vaccinations to be reported to state or New York City immunization registries within 72 hours, while waiving adults' consent for such reporting. Vaccination itself still requires the consent of the patient or a legal guardian. The emergency took effect on Monday and runs through November 4.

item.title: Tate brothers used 'lover boy' model to exploit women, Britain says
item.description: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate used a "lover boy" model to lure women with the promise of romantic relationships before coercing them to create online pornography, British law enforcement said in court documents made public on Monday in the US.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: Social media influencers [USN:L6N451155 TEXT:"Andrew and Tristan Tate"] used a "lover boy" model to lure women with the promise of romantic relationships before coercing them to create online pornography, British law enforcement said in court documents made public on Monday in the US. In the most comprehensive description of the [USN:L6N44O0VS TEXT:"British criminal case"] against the brothers to date, a British detective said the basis of the prosecutors' case was that the brothers encouraged women to travel to their base in Romania with the promise of romantic relationships, before using violence and threats to manipulate them into creating porn. The Tate brothers, who have dual US and British citizenship, were arrested in Miami in July after Britain requested their extradition from the US. The brothers have not appeared in a British court to formally answer to the charges they face, which include rape and human trafficking, but they have denied wrongdoing. Joseph McBride, a lawyer for the Tate brothers, said the accusations could not be "meaningfully tested" because Britain had not disclosed the names of the accusers to the defense. "No American court should be asked to surrender a person to a foreign country on the word of secret accusers," McBride said in a statement. The arrests of Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, marked a new phase in the legal troubles for the former kickboxers, who have built a large online following promoting their views on masculinity and wealth. Andrew Tate has previously described himself as a misogynist. The British embassy in Washington last month sent the United States a series of documents in support of its extradition requests. Those documents included summaries of the cases against the brothers written by a detective with the Bedfordshire Police. According to the summary, Andrew Tate persuaded vulnerable women he had formed relationships with to relocate to Romania by telling them they could earn money by taking part in his webcam business. Once they arrived, the women became financially dependent on the Tate brothers, who often confiscated their passports, the summary read. "The prosecution case is that Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate used and threatened physical and sexual violence in order to maintain control and compliance," the summary read. The Tate brothers have been jailed in Miami since their arrests. US Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis on Thursday asked their lawyers to propose dates for their final extradition hearings, but no date has been set. The brothers have also been under investigation since 2022 in Romania on charges including human trafficking.

item.title: Mattel investor Ariel pushes for sale as turnaround stalls
item.description: A major Mattel shareholder urged the Barbie maker on Monday to explore a sale, saying progress in its performance and profitability had stalled, according to a letter seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Juveria Tabassum, Angela M
item.content:encoded: A major Mattel (MAT.O) shareholder urged the Barbie maker on Monday to explore a sale, saying progress in its performance and profitability had stalled, according to a letter seen by Reuters. Ariel Investments, which holds a 5.4% stake in Mattel, said the company's shares remain significantly undervalued. "By our estimates, a strategic buyer would pay a significant premium to your current share price," Ariel Co-CEO John Rogers said in the letter to Mattel's board. The asset manager said Mattel's options included a "divestiture of significant assets, a merger and/or an outright sale of the company." Other toy companies were likely to find the Mattel portfolio attractive, Ariel said, as were entertainment companies and traditional private equity firms. Mattel has grappled with choppy sales and higher input costs over the past couple of years as its business stabilized following big gains from the popularity of the "Barbie" movie. Its operating income has declined in the last six quarters. Shares of the company were up 0.9% at $16.2 in extended trading. Ariel's push comes as Mattel also undergoes a [USN:L6N45M0SD TEXT:"leadership transition"]. Its boss Ynon Kreiz stepped down late last month, taking on the role of co-CEO at Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) . Mattel's board member Roger Lynch, who was the head of Vogue and the New Yorker owner Condé Nast, will take over as the toymaker's CEO next month. "Our board of directors and management team are committed to acting in the best interests of all shareholders and will consider the views expressed in Ariel Investments' letter, as well as the views of Mattel's other shareholders," Mattel said in an emailed response to Reuters. This is the second time this year that an investor has asked Mattel to consider strategic options. In May, Mattel investor Southeastern Asset Management called on the company [USN:L4N41L0QB TEXT:"to explore options"], including going private, or being acquired by rival Hasbro (HAS.O) or a large media company that would value Mattel's assets better than the public market. Last week, Mattel was [USN:L4N45N1E2 TEXT:"approached"] by Authentic Brands Group (AUTH.N) for a takeover, potentially valuing the toymaker at around $6 billion or more, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. There is no guarantee that Mattel will be open to Authentic Brands' approach, and there is no formal sale process ongoing for the company, the source had said. Mattel's shares soared after the news. Despite that rally, the stock has lost a fifth of its value this year. The toymaker trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings ratio of 9.99, compared with an industry average of 14.03, according to LSEG data. "I think there's just some frustration that maybe the business has stalled a little bit and it would be a good time, given where the valuation is, to perhaps turn this business around away from investor eyes," Morningstar analyst Jaime Katz said.

item.title: McKesson, CD&R near $5 billion-plus deal to buy Option Care, FT reports
item.description: Drug distributor McKesson and private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice are nearing a deal to acquire infusion services provider Option Care Health in a transaction valued at more than $5 billion including debt, the Financial Times reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Sahil Pandey
item.content:encoded: Drug distributor McKesson (MCK.N) and private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice are nearing a deal to acquire infusion services provider Option Care Health in a transaction valued at more than $5 billion including debt, the Financial Times reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. Option Care's shares rose 21% in extended trading following the report. The deal could be announced as soon as Tuesday, although talks could still fall apart, the report said. The possible acquisition would mark McKesson's latest deal as it seeks to expand its healthcare services footprint. In August, the company agreed to buy Precision Medicine Group for about [USN:L4N44M0SS TEXT:"$2.25 billion"] as part of a years-long effort to strengthen higher-growth businesses. Leerink Partners analyst Michael Cherny said the "strategic rationale" for a deal made sense, as it would expand McKesson's reach beyond physician offices into home and alternate-site care settings. Option Care provides infusion services that allow patients to receive intravenous medications at home or in other outpatient settings rather than in hospitals. McKesson had been [USN:L3N3V50X3 TEXT:"reshaping its portfolio"] by exiting non-core assets and investing in areas such as oncology and specialty care. Revenue in its oncology & multispecialty segment rose 33% in the latest reported quarter, helped by growth in specialty distribution and contributions from acquisitions. McKesson declined to comment, while CD&R and Option Care did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the report.

item.title: Cuba and US maintain 'channels of communication' but no negotiations, diplomat says
item.description: Cuba and the United States have maintained “channels of communication” but are not engaged in any formal negotiations, Havana’s top diplomat in Washington told Reuters, as the Trump administration pursues a pressure campaign against the Communist-ruled island.
item.dc:creator: Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: Cuba and the United States have maintained “channels of communication” but are not engaged in any formal negotiations, Havana’s top diplomat in Washington told Reuters, as the Trump administration pursues a pressure campaign against the Communist-ruled island. In an interview on Monday, Lianys Torres Rivera, chargé d’affaires at the embassy in Washington, said Cuba remains open to a “respectful” dialogue but is “not naive” about President Donald Trump’s threats and has increased preparations to defend itself against any US military action. The latest US-Cuba diplomatic contacts have included meetings, phone calls and WhatsApp messages, but the two sides have made no progress toward a negotiating agenda or restarting official talks, she said. “What we have with the US is channels of communication,” Torres Rivera said. She declined to provide details on the timing, topics and participants. Her description of the communications appears to fall short of Trump’s assertion at the United Nations last month that Secretary of State Marco Rubio was “deep into negotiations” with Havana. Trump also called Cuba a [USN:L1N45E0LQ TEXT:""failed state”"] and predicted its government would fall. The Cuban delegation walked out in protest. A US State Department spokesperson said: "It does not come to our surprise that the Cuban regime is circulating this propaganda. In all reality, talks are ongoing and the regime has been unwilling thus far to agree to anything that would help the Cuban people, ultimately, threatening its total control.” Trump has openly stated that his goal is to fundamentally change Cuba's government. A US-imposed [USN:L1N45O0GT TEXT:"oil blockade"] has put the country under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and blackouts exacerbated by failing infrastructure. UN human rights experts have condemned the oil blockade as a violation of international law. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said at the end of June that talks initiated earlier this year with the US had stalled, and in early September that [USN:S0N44Z000 TEXT:"no talks were under way"] or planned. CUBA'S 'RED LINE' Torres Rivera said Cuba’s “red line” remains that Havana is unwilling to negotiate any changes in its political system, seeing Trump’s demands for the removal of the Cuban leadership as a violation of sovereignty. She rejected the Trump administration’s claims that Cuba was a threat to US national security or is interfering in US domestic affairs, and said Washington was using such accusations as a pretext to continue squeezing the island economically in what she called “collective punishment.” A US official, responding to Reuters questions, reiterated Trump's assertion that “we will not allow a haven for foreign adversaries to threaten America on our own doorstep.” The Trump administration tightened the embargo against Cuba last week, further restricting travel there by Americans and access to US banking for its private sector. Those measures, said Torres Rivera, contradict US insistence that it wants Cuba to [USN:L1N45I063 TEXT:"expand private enterprise"]. Facing US pressure, Cuba unveiled [USN:L1N42Q0N1 TEXT:"free-market reforms"] in June that, if fully implemented, would represent the biggest change to the island's socialist economy since former leader Fidel Castro took control in 1959. But Washington says the reforms do not go far enough and has also called for "free and fair" elections. Despite the gaps, Trump predicted late last month that the US and Cuba “will make a deal,” adding, ”I [USN:L1N45I041 TEXT:"don't think we'll need the military"].” But the Cuban government remains wary. “Cuba has always been preparing for an aggression from the US,” Torres Rivera said. “And we are increasing our capabilities now more than ever before … It is to defend ourselves.”

item.title: Trump says US will help Russia after Siberia plague institute death
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday at the White House told reporters that the United States will help Russia after a laboratory worker died at a plague research institute in Siberia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Monday at the White House told reporters that the United States will help Russia after a laboratory worker died at a plague research institute in Siberia. Trump told reporters as he left the White House for a trip to Nebraska that the outbreak is a "big problem for Russia." A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people. The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but Russian authorities said on Monday the situation was under control. "Well, I hate to see them having it," Trump said. "It's a rough disease." He said the US would do what it could to help Russia. Trump has said he considers Russian President Vladimir Putin someone whom he can work with despite tensions over Russia's war against Ukraine. "We'll help," Trump said. "Anybody that has that kind of a problem, we're always will to help."

item.title: Genmab, AbbVie blood cancer drug combo cuts risk of progression or death in late-stage study
item.description: Danish biotech firm Genmab and US drugmaker AbbVie said on Monday their combination treatment for patients newly diagnosed with a type of lymphoma reduced the risk of disease progression or death in a late-stage study.
item.dc:creator: Sahil Pandey
item.content:encoded: Danish biotech firm Genmab (GMAB.CO) and US drugmaker AbbVie (ABBV.N) said on Monday their combination treatment for patients newly diagnosed with a type of lymphoma reduced the risk of disease progression or death in a late-stage study. US-listed shares of Genmab were up about 1.04% in extended trading. AbbVie's shares were flat. The study tested epcoritamab in combination with R-CHOP in newly diagnosed patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), the most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma The combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 51% in newly diagnosed patients compared with R-CHOP alone, the companies said Barclays analyst Emily Field said the result was a strong validation of epcoritamab in frontline DLBCL, which represents the largest commercial opportunity for the drug Epcoritamab, jointly developed by Genmab and AbbVie, is an immune-based therapy that helps the body's T cells attack cancer cells, while R-CHOP is currently offered as the standard treatment for those with DLBCL The companies said the trial is the first late-stage study of a bispecific antibody combination to significantly improve progression-free survival — how long patients live without their cancer worsening — in first-line DLBCL They said the combination's safety profile was generally consistent with the known safety profiles of epcoritamab and R-CHOP Epcoritamab has not yet been approved for patients who have just been diagnosed and have not received prior treatment

item.title: Pennsylvania measles cases rise to 1,004 as outbreak spreads
item.description: Pennsylvania's health department reported 1,004 measles cases as of Monday, as the state grapples with a fast-growing outbreak.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pennsylvania's health department reported 1,004 measles cases as of Monday, as the state grapples with a fast-growing outbreak. Five Pennsylvania residents have [USN:L4N45M1NB TEXT:"died"] after contracting the highly contagious disease, as cases in the US reach their highest level in more than three decades. The Pennsylvania measles cases include 198 hospitalizations, according to the health department's website Lancaster county remains the hardest-hit area in the state with 391 cases All five people who have died from the disease in Pennsylvania this year were unvaccinated The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed only [USN:L4N45L13A TEXT:"two measles-related deaths"] in the country this year, without naming the states The CDC has recorded 3,887 measles cases in 2026 so far — the most since the major resurgence between 1989 and 1991, when 55,000 infections and 123 deaths were recorded The CDC has said it was working with state epidemiologists on a standard definition for measles-related deaths Measles is a highly contagious viral disease but preventable with the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine, which is 97% effective after two doses

item.title: Reports: Seahawks to sign RB Joe Mixon
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are signing veteran running back Joe Mixon after he worked out for the team on Monday, according to several reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks are signing veteran running back Joe Mixon after he worked out for the team on Monday, according to several reports. Seattle coach Mike Macdonald indicated Mixon would start out on the practice squad. "We're down runners," Macdonald said. "We need running backs. He's a good running back." Before adding Mixon, the defending champs' only healthy running backs were Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Velus Jones. The Seahawks (3-1) placed rookie running back Jadarian Price, the 32nd overall pick in April's draft, on injured reserve Saturday with a chest injury. Zach Charbonnet will get work in team drills during practice this week but won't play Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers, Macdonald said. Mixon, 30, is a two-time Pro Bowler who last played for the Houston Texans in 2024 following seven seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals. He racked up 1,016 yards, 11 touchdowns and a Pro Bowl nod in his 14 games for the Texans. But Mixon missed the 2025 campaign due to a leg injury and was released last March. Mixon has gained 7,428 yards and scored 60 touchdowns on the ground in 111 career games (102 starts) since entering the league in 2017. He has added another 2,448 yards and 14 touchdowns on 319 receptions. Charbonnet, 25, has yet to make his season debut after tearing his ACL on Jan. 17 in the NFC Divisional Round defeat of the 49ers on Seattle's path to a Super Bowl championship. The second-round pick (52nd overall) in the 2023 NFL Draft ran for a career-high 730 yards and 12 touchdowns last season. He has rushed for 1,761 yards and 21 touchdowns while catching 95 passes for 693 yards and one touchdown in 49 games (eight starts) in three years for the Seahawks. Macdonald also shared that All-Pro defensive lineman Leonard Williams' status is up in the air for the San Francisco game after sustaining an ankle injury in the Seahawks' 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Williams, 32, was a Pro Bowler in each of his first two full seasons in Seattle and has 39 tackles for loss and 25 sacks in 47 games (all starts) with the Seahawks. "We are optimistic, and we will see this week," Macdonald said of Williams' status. --Field Level Media

item.title: McDonald's hit with class action alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing
item.description: McDonald's has been sued in federal court in Chicago in a proposed nationwide class action alleging the fast-food company illegally coordinates menu prices across its franchises and company-owned restaurants through an AI-powered pricing system.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: McDonald's (MCD.N) has been sued in federal court in Chicago in a proposed nationwide class action alleging the fast-food company illegally coordinates menu prices across its franchises and company-owned restaurants through an AI-powered pricing system. The lawsuit , filed on Friday, said McDonald’s violated US antitrust law by conspiring with independent franchisees to fix prices using algorithms trained on nonpublic data. Reuters [USN:L6N45K103 TEXT:"reported last week"] that McDonald’s pricing engine uses machine-learning algorithms to continually analyze data from millions of daily transactions across its nearly 14,000 restaurants. The lawsuit cited the Reuters article, which said other fast-food companies are also turning to AI to help with pricing and other operations. "Independent businesses must set their prices independently," the lawsuit said. McDonald’s, in a statement on Monday, called the allegations speculative and uninformed. "AI does not set the price of a Big Mac or any other menu item," the company said. It said franchisees make their own pricing decisions, and that the use of pricing recommendation tools and analytics is widespread across industries. US plaintiffs have filed a wave of class actions in recent years alleging that companies used algorithms or AI to illegally coordinate prices for hotel rooms, apartment rentals and other purchases. Lark Turner, a lawyer for the plaintiff, said in a statement, that McDonald's is "leveraging its troves of data and its franchised system to nickel-and-dime consumers down to the last French fry." The plaintiff, an Illinois resident, is seeking to represent a class of potentially millions of McDonald's customers, the lawsuit said.

item.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI's rogue agents possibly tied to data service disruption in May
item.description: The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said heavy traffic from OpenAI's rogue agents was possibly tied to a disruption that its data service experienced in May.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said heavy traffic from OpenAI's rogue agents was possibly tied to a disruption that its data service experienced in May. In a blog post on Monday , Wikimedia said it could confirm "that we have discovered some activity by these 'rogue' OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms," including a May incident that resulted in a "partial outage" of its Wikidata Query Service. Wikimedia said the disruption seemed to have been triggered as the agents visited millions of pages and made hundreds of thousands of data queries. Wikimedia also said the OpenAI agents made unauthorized edits to Wikimedia wiki sites, including "potentially malicious edits" to a citation tool, which the foundation said were likely intended to hijack it. Wikimedia said its Etherpad note-taking tool was also hit by malicious activity from OpenAI's agents. OpenAI said in a statement that it appreciated Wikimedia's "detailed findings" and was working with the organization to analyze the activity. "We’ll continue to share relevant information as that work progresses," OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said. OpenAI has been scrambling to get its arms around the full scope of its rogue agent activity, [USN:L6N45H0LE TEXT:"Reuters has previously reported"].

item.title: Report: Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov (leg) out 10-12 weeks
item.description: Florida Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov is set to be sidelined for 10 to 12 weeks with the left leg injury that landed him on long-term injured reserve, according to a report by Locked On Panthers on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Florida Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov is set to be sidelined for 10 to 12 weeks with the left leg injury that landed him on long-term injured reserve, according to a report by Locked On Panthers on Monday. However, Panthers coach Paul Maurice appeared to refute the report when asked about Barkov's timeline later Monday. "Do not bet your hard-earned money on that one," Maurice said, adding that Barkov is still meeting with doctors and the team will have another update Tuesday. "I know you can bet on everything these days, but hang on to your cash. ... If I don't know, nobody else does." Barkov sustained the injury during the second period of Florida's 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Thursday. He was vying for the puck along the boards when he was pushed by Sharks defenseman Darnell Nurse, causing Barkov to fall to the ice with his knee at an awkward angle. Barkov remained on the ice for several moments before retreating to the locker room. It was just Barkov's second game back after he missed the entire 2025-26 season due to torn ligaments in his right knee. He was placed on long-term IR Saturday, meaning he'll be forced to miss a minimum of 10 games. The reported timeline would align with Barkov returning to action in mid-December or early January. Barkov, 31, is a two-time Stanley Cup winner and a three-time Selke Trophy recipient (2021, 2024, 2025) as the NHL's best defensive forward, leading the Panthers to consecutive Stanley Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. He boasts franchise records for goals (286), assists (496), points (782) and games played (806) since being selected with the second overall pick of the 2013 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rendimientos de bonos Tesoro EEUU a largo plazo suben por percepción pesimista sobre la deuda
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense subieron en su mayoría el lunes, debido al pesimismo que prevalecía en el mercado de deuda, mientras los inversores sopesan las perspectivas de un alza de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense subieron en su mayoría el lunes, debido al pesimismo que prevalecía en el mercado de deuda, mientras los inversores sopesan las perspectivas de un alza de las tasas de interés. Los rendimientos se mantuvieron al alza después de que datos económicos sugirieron que la inflación podría permanecer alta hasta 2027. Un informe del Instituto de Gerencia y Abastecimiento (ISM, por su sigla en inglés) mostró que la actividad del sector servicios estadounidense se ralentizó en septiembre, mientras que la fuerte demanda interna ejerció presión sobre las cadenas de suministro e impulsó los precios que pagan las empresas por los insumos a máximos de más de cuatro años. "No hubo nada que impulsara los rendimientos en la dirección contraria", dijo Jim Barnes, director de renta fija de Bryn Mawr Trust. Las preocupaciones fiscales en el extranjero también siguieron lastrando el mercado de bonos estadounidense, añadió. "Es ese asunto general el que se cierne sobre el mercado de bonos: las preocupaciones fiscales en todo el mundo en diversos mercados desarrollados", explicó. "Cuando surge en algún lugar… empieza a influir en los mercados de bonos de todo el mundo, y hoy estamos viendo algo de eso". Los precios de los bonos han caído en todo el mundo, lo que ha provocado un aumento de los rendimientos, y suscitado preocupación por la deuda pública en Francia y de otros países. Los rendimientos en España subieron el lunes después de que el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, convocó elecciones anticipadas para el 29 de noviembre en un intento de reforzar su mandato, tras el rechazo por parte del Parlamento de los decretos del Gobierno sobre vivienda la semana pasada, en un contexto de las protestas. Las probabilidades de una subida de tasas de interés este mes se vieron reducidas por los recientes datos de inflación inferiores a lo esperado en agosto y julio, así como por la desaceleración del crecimiento del empleo no agrícola en Estados Unidos durante septiembre. El viernes, los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense revirtieron sus caídas anteriores, a pesar de un informe de empleo de septiembre que resultó ser más débil de lo esperado. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME Group, los operadores estimaban una probabilidad de aproximadamente el 76% de que las tasas se mantengan sin cambios en la reunión de este mes. Las expectativas de una subida en diciembre superan el 80%. El mes pasado, la Reserva Federal subió las tasas de interés por primera vez desde 2023 en un intento por controlar la inflación. El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años subió 3,4 puntos básicos, al 5,311%. El rendimiento del bono a 30 años ganó 3,2 puntos básicos, al 5,662%. En la sesión, el bono a 10 años alcanzó el 5,3493% y el de 30 años el 5,7029%, ambos nuevos máximos en 24 años. La diferencia entre los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a dos y diez años , considerado un indicador de las expectativas económicas, se situó en 48,8 puntos básicos, tras haber estado en 49,70, su nivel más alto desde el 21 de agosto. El retorno del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a dos años , que normalmente se mueve en línea con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal, bajó 0,4 puntos básicos, al 4,821%.

item.title: Trump expands access to tax-exempt diesel fuel
item.description: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that he unveiled from a rally stage in Nebraska.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that he unveiled from a [USN:L1N45R0ZC TEXT:"rally stage in Nebraska"]. High diesel prices, which shot to a record of about $6.50 a gallon last month, are a risk to Trump ahead of the November 3 midterm US elections in which control of Congress is at stake. Trump's Republican Party currently holds a narrow majority in the Senate and House of Representatives. Prices for the fuel integral to trucking goods have risen in response to the US-Israeli war on Iran and the Russian invasion of Ukraine , with the conflicts having led to attacks on refineries in the Middle East and Russia. Trump said the directive will waive the off-road requirement for tax-free diesel and allow anyone to buy the red dye diesel fuel that is used by the agriculture industry and by some off-road vehicles. "We are not going to need it long, I hope," Trump said of the waiver. The order released by the White House directs the treasury secretary, in consultation with the Pentagon chief, "to defer payment of the federal excise tax imposed for on-road use of dyed diesel fuel for the remainder of the year without interest or penalties, and to explore pathways to eliminate the obligation to pay the deferred taxes." It also directs the US agriculture secretary to "ensure farmers' access to dyed diesel in high-demand areas" while asking the transportation secretary to coordinate with states, industry leadership, and labor organizations on access to dyed diesel. G7 countries announced last week that they would release 100 million barrels of diesel, after pressure from Trump who had considered banning US exports of the fuel. But it was not clear how much of that release would be entirely new supplies or compliance with a global agreement in March. Trump's approval rating held [USN:L6N45R122 TEXT:"at a record-low"] 32% in recent days, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday, with Americans most concerned about the high cost of living, spurred by soaring gasoline and diesel prices due to the US war on Iran.

item.title: Plaza financiera argentina recupera fortaleza por resultado electoral en el vecino Brasil
item.description: La plaza financiera de Argentina operó con un alza generalizada el lunes en línea con la victoria electoral de la derecha en Brasil, un factor que ayuda a movilizar liquidez.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera de Argentina operó con un alza generalizada el lunes en línea con la victoria electoral de la derecha en Brasil, un factor que ayuda a movilizar liquidez. El optimismo inversor se adueñó de toda la región sudamericana, impactando de lleno en el riesgo país argentino que se retrotrajo por debajo de la línea de los 600 puntos. La mejora de precios se anotó tras importantes caídas recientes en el mercado doméstico, apoyada por una demanda liderada en papeles del sector financiero y en bonos atados a dólares. Brasil, principal socio comercial de Argentina, celebró [USN:L1N45R01Q TEXT:"comicios presidenciales el domingo"], donde se definió que el senador Flávio Bolsonaro se enfrentará a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en el balotaje que se llevará a cabo el 25 de octubre. La mayoría de las encuestas preveían este panorama, pero con Lula ganador en la primera ronda. El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires subió un 3,68% al cierre, donde se destacaron las mejoras de los papeles de los bancos BBVA (BBARm.BA) y Macro (BMAm.BA) con un 5,63% y 5,24%, respectivamente. Este mercado en particular viene de retroceder un 4,36% la semana previa y de finalizar septiembre con una pronunciada merma de 7,07%. "Consideramos que el resultado electoral de ayer (domingo) en Brasil es favorable para Argentina. La ventaja de dos puntos de Bolsonaro lo deja al borde de una victoria, y creemos que un real más fuerte, tasas más bajas y la presencia de un aliado natural dentro del Mercosur juegan a favor de los planes del presidente (argentino Javier) Milei", afirmó la consultora Max Capital. En tanto, el peso argentino interbancario se apreció muy leve 0,07% a 1.520,5 unidades por dólar para la venta, con la atenta mirada del banco central (BCRA), entidad que absorbió 14 millones de dólares de la plaza cambiaria única. La entidad monetaria, que busca reforzar sus reservas internacionales, adquirió 369 millones de dólares la semana previa y quedó cerca de alcanzar los 15.000 millones de dólares de compras en lo que va del año. Recientemente el secretario del Tesoro estadounidense, Scott Bessent, dejo abierta la posibilidad de volver a ayudar financieramente a Argentina. Bessent "afirmó que Estados Unidos podría repetir la asistencia financiera brindada a Argentina el año pasado. Consultado por Axios en una entrevista sobre la posibilidad de nuevas intervenciones en los mercados financieros, Bessent citó el caso de Argentina y señaló que Estados Unidos podría volver a hacerlo", agregó Max Capital. En octubre de 2025, el Tesoro estadounidense realizó compras de moneda argentina y alcanzó un [USN:L2N3VQ0V6 TEXT:"acuerdo"] para un intercambio de divisas por 20.000 millones de dólares con el BCRA. Los bonos del país austral en el segmento extrabursátil ganaron un 0,9% promedio, mientras que el riesgo país de Argentina se desplomaba a 599 puntos básicos (2130 GMT), luego de alcanzar las 655 unidades el viernes, su máximo nivel en 10 meses. "La suba del riesgo país junto con el mal contexto externo agregan presión al programa financiero 2027. Ahora, para conseguir los 5.000 millones de dólares previstos de emisiones locales, la tasa a convalidar es más del 11% (anual), algo que hasta hace poco era considerado caro", expresó Roberto Geretto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. Por este contexto, los inversores financieras en Argentina muestran una notoria prudencia operativa.

item.title: What to know about Spain's November snap election
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called an early election for November 29 that he hopes will hand him a parliamentary majority but which could just as easily usher in a conservative coalition, as the centre-left bloc trails in most opinion polls.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"called an early election"] for November 29 that he hopes will hand him a parliamentary majority but which could just as easily usher in a conservative coalition, as the centre-left bloc trails in most opinion polls. Here is what you need to know about the election: POLLS PITCH RIGHT-WING COALITION AS LIKELIEST OUTCOME Sanchez's Socialist Party (PSOE) has long trailed in the polls, hovering around 28% and never above 33% throughout his eight years in office. Parties further to the left, which will be key for Sanchez to cobble together a coalition, are currently polling at around 8%. A coalition between the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox is the only combination projected to win enough votes for an absolute majority in the 350-seat lower house of parliament. Voting intention for Vox stands at roughly 18%, propelled by younger and male voters. ISSUES LIKELY TO DOMINATE THE ELECTORAL CAMPAIGN Housing will dominate the left's agenda, with Sanchez taking the decision to call the election after protests erupted across the country following the high-profile eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid home. Immigration is likely to be another defining issue, both for Sanchez as one of Europe's loudest advocates of immigration's benefits for society and the economy, recently [USN:L8N42N0Y2 TEXT:"granting legal status"] to nearly a million undocumented migrants, and for Vox, which wants far tighter controls. The mass crossing of 72,000 migrants [USN:L8N43W1SU TEXT:"into Ceuta in July"] has overwhelmed local authorities and triggered major political disputes over Spain's ability to control its borders. Corruption: Opposition parties are expected to make corruption a central theme of the election campaign, seeking to tie Sanchez to a series of investigations, trials and convictions involving members of his [USN:L8N42U0LE TEXT:"inner circle"] and [USN:L1N42S02V TEXT:"family"]. Sanchez has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and argued that some of the cases form part of a [USN:L1N4260JB TEXT:"politically motivated campaign"] against his government. CANDIDATES FOR PRIME MINISTER Sanchez, the incumbent, will run again for the Socialists, having spearheaded the party since 2017. Now seeking a third term after eight years in office, he is already Spain's second-longest-serving premier since the country returned to democracy in 1978. Despite a tenure dogged in the past two years by [USN:L1N42U0KB TEXT:"corruption investigations"], the Socialist leader is betting that the housing crisis and the prospect of a far-right party coming to power will help mobilise left-leaning voters who might have otherwise abstained. Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, former president of the region of Galicia, will run against Sanchez representing the People's Party, which he has led since April 2022. A four-time winner of presidential elections in Galicia, Feijoo built a reputation in his years governing the region as a moderate and pragmatic administrator. The PP emerged as the largest party in the 2023 general election but failed to secure enough support to form a government, leaving Feijoo as leader of the opposition. Since then, Feijoo has sought to position the PP as a government-in-waiting, piling criticism on Sanchez for everything from his policies to the corruption allegations encircling his party. A CABINET ROLE FOR THE FAR RIGHT? Polls project that the PP would rely on far-right Vox to govern, giving a far-right party a role in cabinet for the first time since the death of former dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Its leader is Santiago Abascal, who built his political profile in the Basque Country opposing separatism and co-founded the party in 2014 alongside others defecting from or seeking an alternative to the PP. Under Abascal, Vox has evolved from a minor political force into the country's third-largest party. It advocates tougher immigration controls, recentralisation of state powers, lower taxes and the reversal of many progressive social policies. A MOBILISED LEFT? THE 'BROAD FRONT' A swathe of parties to the left of PSOE are planning to launch a new common platform called "Broad Front" (Frente Amplio), which will be Sanchez's best hope of maintaining power if it supports the Socialists in coalition as previously. The alliance would replace Sumar, a hard-left platform founded in 2023 by Labour Minister Yolanda Diaz which acted as coalition partner to Sanchez's government in his final term. The new front will name a leadership candidate at a launch event on October 17, after Diaz said she would not stand as leader again. Podemos, former junior coalition partners to PSOE who take a more critical line than Sumar, has for now refused to join the front, opting to run separately unless open primaries are held. OTHER PARTIES Spain's parliament is highly fragmented, giving minor parties that hold just a handful of seats the power to tip the scales on passing policy. The country's historically distinct regions feature four separatist parties: EH Bildu in the Basque Country, BNG in Galicia, and two in Catalonia — the left-leaning ERC and the right-leaning Junts. While EH Bildu, BNG and ERC have broadly supported Sanchez, Junts has frequently vetoed his government's measures, including the housing decrees that prompted the prime minister to dissolve parliament.

item.title: BIS chief warns soaring debt, market changes could complicate future crisis response
item.description: Central banks will remain at the heart of managing future financial crises, but rising public debt and other key changes could make their task more difficult and controversial, the head of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: Central banks will remain at the heart of managing future financial crises, but rising public debt and other key changes could make their task more difficult and controversial, the head of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said on Monday. Speaking in Vienna, Pablo Hernández de Cos - one of the frontrunners to take over from Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank President next year, said the run of crises over the last 20 years had demonstrated the importance of swift central bank action in quelling market turmoil. However, he said the backdrop for the next crisis was changing rapidly. Public debt levels are near post-World War Two highs in many economies, while budget deficits remain large and fiscal pressures are expected to persist. That could make it harder for central banks to distinguish between market dysfunction requiring intervention and legitimate investor concerns over government finances. "If market dysfunction threatens financial stability or monetary transmission, central banks need to intervene," Hernández de Cos said. "But when debt is high and public financing needs are large, even a well-designed operation can be interpreted through a fiscal lens". CRISIS-MANAGEMENT TOOLS The BIS chief's warnings come amid a sharp recent rise in bond yields globally and as an [USN:L8N45O0YO TEXT:"explosion"] of the 'spread' - or gap - between French yields and those of triple-A rated Germany , stirs memories of the euro crisis. Hernández de Cos also highlighted the growing influence of so-called 'non-bank financial institutions' such as hedge funds, pension funds and asset managers, which have become major holders of government debt. While they support market liquidity in normal times, their use of leverage and market-based funding can amplify stress during periods of turmoil, he said, pointing to the March 2020 "dash for cash" in US Treasury markets and Britain's 2022 gilt market crisis as evidence. He said the Bank of England’s response "offers a blueprint" for how central banks should use asset purchases as a crisis-fighting tool. Strictly limited purchase windows and amounts as well as clear communication and governance mechanisms worked well, he said, although he also warned that in a bigger and more persistent crisis, "such commitment might not be credible". He added that online banking, social media, stablecoins and AI could all increase the speed of future crises. Rapid online withdrawals and the fast spread of information, including misinformation, could force policymakers to respond more quickly than in the past. He argued that stronger regulation of non-banks and emerging financial technologies would be needed to limit moral hazard and preserve the effectiveness of central bank crisis-management tools. "Central banks have a key role to play, but so do regulators and governments," Hernández de Cos said, adding that "global cooperation" also remained crucial. "Central bank swap lines remain critical to stabilise the global financial system at times of acute distress."

item.title: Açúcar bruto atinge maior cotação em 19 meses; café também sobe
item.description: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE subiram 4% nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 20 centavos por libra-peso e atingindo a maior cotação em 19 meses, à medida que aumentavam as preocupações com novas chuvas excessivas relacionadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE subiram 4% nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 20 centavos por libra-peso e atingindo a maior cotação em 19 meses, à medida que aumentavam as preocupações com novas chuvas excessivas relacionadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor. AÇÚCAR * O primeiro contrato fechou com alta de 0,8 centavo, ou 4%, a 20,73 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir a máxima de 19 meses de 20,81 centavos. O contrato registrou alta de 7,7% na semana passada. * "Dadas as chuvas recordes em setembro... e a perspectiva de mais chuvas ao longo de outubro, parece que o mercado está convencido de que a produção de açúcar ficará bem abaixo das estimativas", afirmaram analistas da Green Pool. * A produção brasileira caiu 41,6% na primeira quinzena de setembro devido ao excesso de chuvas. Também há alguns atrasos no carregamento de açúcar nos portos brasileiros devido às condições climáticas, segundo corretores. * Espera-se que o El Niño afete negativamente as safras nos três principais produtores de açúcar -- Brasil, Índia e Tailândia. A próxima safra da União Europeia também deve cair drasticamente devido à seca deste verão. * O contrato de açúcar branco subiu 3%, para US$547,60 por tonelada métrica, após atingir a maior cotação desde o final de agosto, em US$ 552,50. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou com alta de 3,8 centavos, ou 1,3%, a US$2,9255 por libra-peso, após ter subido 3,6% na semana passada. * O café arábica tem sido impulsionado no curto prazo por preocupações com a qualidade, devido ao excesso de chuvas associadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor, e pelo temor de que o padrão climático possa causar seca no futuro. * David Behrends, da Sucafina, disse que, embora ainda se espere uma safra abundante no Brasil em 2026/27, alguns participantes do mercado permanecem "altistas" no curto prazo devido aos estoques reduzidos e aos preços físicos elevados na Colômbia e na América Central. * Os corretores observaram um salto de quase 5% na moeda brasileira, o real, na segunda-feira, após os resultados das eleições aumentarem as chances do candidato presidencial de direita Flávio Bolsonaro. Uma moeda local mais forte geralmente desacelera as vendas dos produtores. * O preço do café robusta subiu 1,7%, para US$3.528 por tonelada. * O Vietnã, maior produtor de robusta, exportou 1,45 milhão de toneladas métricas de café nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, um aumento de 16,2%. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou com alta de £143 , ou 3,4%, a £4.382 por tonelada. * Os corretores afirmaram que o cacau permanece, em geral, dentro de uma faixa estreita, preso entre o excesso de oferta atual e uma perspectiva cada vez mais desfavorável para a safra 2026/27, associada ao El Niño. * A safra principal da Costa do Marfim deve cair cerca de 17% nesta temporada, de acordo com uma pesquisa da Reuters, enquanto os agricultores marfinenses afirmaram nesta segunda-feira que a escassez de chuvas amplia o risco de encurtar a safra principal, que vai de setembro a fevereiro. * As chegadas de cacau aos portos da Costa do Marfim totalizaram 18.000 toneladas métricas na semana encerrada em 4 de outubro, elevando o total desde o início da safra 2025/26 para 54.500 toneladas. * O contrato de futuros de cacau de Nova York subiu 3,5%, para US$5.867 por tonelada. (Por May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes, killing 32
item.description: A Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew members.
item.dc:creator: Camillus Eboh, Macdonald Dzirutwe
item.content:encoded: A Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew members. President Bola Tinubu, confirming that there were no survivors, expressed "profound sadness" and extended condolences to the families of those aboard. "The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences," Tinubu said in a statement. The Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact with it at 0813 GMT on Monday, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. The accident was one of the deadliest air disasters in Nigeria in recent years. The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, where search and rescue teams were deployed.

item.title: US Supreme Court won't hear Zillow's bid to escape investor class action
item.description: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by real estate platform Zillow Group to escape a class action that accused it of misleading investors about its failed home-flipping venture.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by real estate platform Zillow Group (ZG.O) to escape a class action that accused it of misleading investors about its failed home-flipping venture. The court turned away Seattle-based Zillow's appeal of a lower court's decision that allowed the 2021 lawsuit to move forward in federal court in Washington state. "We look forward to now moving this case to trial," said Steve Berman, a lawyer at the Hagens Berman law firm which brought the class action. Zillow did not respond to a request for comment. At issue in the case is what defenses publicly traded companies can raise in lawsuits alleging they made false statements to the investing public. In such class actions, which are common in US courts, plaintiffs' lawyers frequently allege that companies made misrepresentations designed not to actively drive up their stock price, but simply to keep it from falling. The Zillow dispute is an example of one of these cases, known as "price-maintenance" cases. Zillow's stock plunged in November 2021 because the company announced it was permanently shutting down Zillow Offers, its home-flipping division, after management admitted it could not accurately forecast future home prices. The company disclosed that it wrote down $300 million in losses during the previous quarter and announced a layoff of 25% of its workforce. Investors sued in federal court, saying statements made by Zillow's then-CEO and other company leaders in the preceding months painted an overly positive picture of the business unit. Zillow's lawyers denied that the company had engaged in securities fraud. "Zillow made a business decision to enter a new line of business, disclosing all of the risk in doing so, that in the end simply did not work out as the company had hoped," Zillow's lawyers said in a court filing. The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals last year upheld a judge's decision that allowed the case to move forward as a class action. The disclosures Zillow made in November 2021 "revealed new information about how Zillow's home-pricing struggles threatened the business and suggested that its earlier statements may have obscured how Zillow's pricing model misfired," the 9th Circuit said. In a filing asking the Supreme Court to hear its appeal, Zillow said the justices should clear up a split in federal appellate courts over how closely related a company's back-end corrective disclosures, which trigger a stock drop, must be to earlier alleged misstatements to justify certifying a class action. Pro-business lobbying groups including the US Chamber of Commerce have criticized the 9th Circuit decision, saying in a filing that this ruling deviated from Supreme Court precedent and "would expose American businesses to costly securities class-action lawsuits."

item.title: Yémen Les forces gouvernementales ont lancé une offensive sur Sanaa, progressent vers Bab el-Mandeb
item.description: Les forces armées gouvernementales yéménites ont annoncé lundi avoir lancé une "offensive stratégique" sur Sanaa, la capitale du Yémen, afin de reprendre le contrôle de la ville aux mains des rebelles houthis pro-iraniens.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Mohammed Ghobari
item.content:encoded: Les forces armées gouvernementales yéménites ont annoncé lundi avoir lancé une "offensive stratégique" sur Sanaa, la capitale du Yémen, afin de reprendre le contrôle de la ville aux mains des rebelles houthis pro-iraniens. Les forces gouvernementales, soutenues par l'Arabie saoudite, avaient atteint lundi les abords de la ville portuaire de Mocha, les combattants houthistes se retirant dans les terres, selon quatre sources gouvernementales. Le ministre de la Défense a confirmé que la ville située sur la mer Rouge était tombée. Les forces gouvernementales yéménites se sont également emparées de positions clés dans le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, ont indiqué des sources militaires et gouvernementales, alors que les Houthis ont avancé le mois dernier vers cette voie navigable stratégique. Une grande partie du district de Dhoubab, qui surplombe Bab el-Mandeb, est désormais sous le contrôle de l'armée yéménite, grâce à un soutien aérien massif de la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite, ont déclaré à Reuters trois sources militaires et une source gouvernementale. Le ministre yéménite de l'Information, Moammar al-Eryani, a précisé à Reuters que l'armée gouvernementale s'était emparée de la piste d'atterrissage de Dhoubab. Située sur le littoral occidental, Dhoubab abrite une base militaire à une trentaine de kilomètres du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, verrou vers la mer Rouge. Une source militaire gouvernementale affirme toutefois que des combats se poursuivent dans et autour de la base où se trouve la piste d'atterrissage. Les forces soutenues par Ryad ont rapporté que leurs forces navales ont mené une opération militaire dans le gouvernorat d'al Hodeïdah contre les combattants houthistes. Dimanche, le président yéménite, Rachad al Alimi, a annoncé le lancement d'une vaste opération militaire visant à reprendre le contrôle des territoires occupés par les Houthis. Les Houthis contrôlent la capitale depuis 2014, ainsi qu'une grande partie du nord-ouest du pays, où vit la majeure partie de la population. Le mouvement aligné sur l'Iran a déclaré dans la soirée avoir mené trois opérations militaires sur le sol saoudien, visant l'aéroport international du roi Khaled de Ryad, une raffinerie Aramco à Rabigh, l'aéroport international d'Abha ainsi que la base militaire de Khamis Mushait. L'Arabie saoudite n'a pas confirmé dans l'immédiat l'existence de ces attaques. Les médias proches des Houthis avaient auparavant nié toute progression des forces gouvernementales dans la région. Le ministère houthiste de la Santé a fait état de deux morts et sept blessés dans des bombardements de l'armée gouvernementale sur Sanhan et Sa'wan, dans la province de Sanaa. Les combats font rage depuis des semaines sur plusieurs fronts au Yémen, alors que la guerre civile, globalement latente depuis 2022, a regagné en intensité avec le conflit entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Les Houthis ont notamment entrepris de prendre le contrôle du détroit stratégique de Bab el-Mandeb, et ont lancé plusieurs attaques contre l'Arabie saoudite - alliée des Etats-Unis - et en mer Rouge depuis leur annonce en juillet dernier d'un blocus maritime des ports saoudiens. Alors que les exportations énergétiques du Golfe sont déjà limitées par la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz par l’Iran, les combats au Yémen menacent cette autre voie énergétique majeure, ce qui a fait grimper les prix mondiaux et fait naître de nouveaux risques. L’Arabie saoudite, qui arme et forme les forces yéménites, soutient la campagne militaire du gouvernement (en exil à Aden)par sa puissance aérienne et a sollicité l’aide logistique de ses alliés pour repousser les Houthis, rétablir la libre circulation en mer Rouge et mettre fin aux attaques sur son territoire. La Turquie et le Pakistan ont discuté avec Ryad du soutien à apporter à leur allié saoudien à l'occasion d'une réunion d'urgence du comité issu du pacte de défense de La Mecque, a annoncé le ministre turc des Affaires étrangères. "Nous avons également discuté de ce qui peut être réalisé pour résoudre le problème pacifiquement à travers le dialogue. L'Arabie saoudite a adopté une approche très constructive pour résoudre le problème", a déclaré Hakan Fidan, à la suite de la réunion. Les trois pays ont par la suite annoncé dans un communiqué commun "le déploiement rapide" de forces militaires en Arabie saoudite. La réunion a permis de "réaffirmer la solidarité et l'unité de nos pays face aux attaques haineuses contre le Royaume et les lieux saints", a réagi le ministère saoudien de la Défense sur X. COMBATS VIOLENTS SE DÉROULENT DANS LE SUD-OUEST DU YÉMEN Les combats les plus violents ces derniers jours ont eu lieu dans le sud-ouest du Yémen, tant dans la zone côtière près du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb qu'autour de la ville de Taïz, dans le sud-ouest, où les Houthis tentent d’encercler les forces gouvernementales. Une agence de presse contrôlée par le groupe rebelle a cité lundi une source militaire affirmant que les Houthis avait chassé les forces gouvernementales du district d’al-Mawasit, dans la province de Taïz, et avait atteint une résidence de Rachad al Alimi. Au cours du week-end, les Houthis ont progressé sur la dernière route reliant Taïz à Aden. La prise de contrôle par les Houthis de la route de Taïz-Aden entraînerait un siège de fait de Taïz, troisième plus grande ville du Yémen, où vivent des centaines de milliers de civils et où sont également stationnés des milliers de soldats des forces gouvernementales.
